summary: Yuan–Zhang prove the averaged Colmez conjecture: the average over CM types of the Faltings heights is −½L_f'(0,η)/L_f(0,η) − ¼log(d_{E/F}d_F). They reduce it to quaternionic Shimura curves, comparing CM component heights with an arithmetic Hodge height (Theorem 1.6) and computing that height by a Gross–Zagier-type kernel and arithmetic adjunction (Theorem 1.7). The 2023 erratum replaces Theorem 2.7 by a weaker statement that suffices. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-three findings are recorded; only E1 (the erratum) affects a stated result, and none affects Theorems 1.1, 1.6 or 1.7. Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18) there are 139 items (6 library, 14 planned, 119 missing) and 55 source issues. The review found further gaps in the printed proof of Theorem 1.6. At primes of F ramified over Q, the τ-quotient arguments of §5.2 and of the erratum's Proposition 6 do not hold as written. Theorems 1.6 and 1.7 need Ô_𝔹 ⊇ Ô_E, which is stronger than the stated hypothesis when a dyadic place of F with residue field F_2 splits in E. Theorem 1.6 is proved only for compact X_U. Theorem 1.1 still holds (AGHMP18 prove it independently), but on this paper's route the ramified-prime gap of §5.2 must be closed first; the other two restrictions are met by choosing the auxiliary datum. Lemmas 7.6(2) and 8.7(2) are false at the places S2, but their errors cancel, so Proposition 9.2(2), Theorem 9.1 and Theorem 1.7 stand.

items.name: CM field and conjugation
items.statement: E is a CM field: a number field with [E:Q] = 2g that is a totally complex quadratic extension of its maximal totally real subfield F ([F:Q] = g). Its complex conjugation c is the nontrivial element of Gal(E/F); τ(c x) = conj(τ(x)) for every embedding τ : E → C, and c² = 1.
api: identify chosen F with maximalRealSubfield E
use complexConj rather than a second involution.
unitTests: Q(i) has real subfield Q and nontrivial involution.
No assertion that c is an element of every local absolute Galois group.
items.note: Pinned declaration statement read; only this precise carrier/lemma is reusable, not the surrounding arithmetic geometry. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper's E is a number field of degree 2g (§1.1, p. 535); 'characteristic-zero' copies the hypotheses of Mathlib's class, which does not itself force finite degree. Harmless, but the item should say number field. Review note: library: checked at 082e2d3. items.statement: If A and B have CM by OE with the same type Φ, then h(A,τ)=h(B,τ) for every τ∈Φ, independently of the integral lattice.

The outline is sound: after the E4 repair the local identity is ∏_σ|α_{στ}|_p = ∏_σ|α_{στc}|_p because σ ↦ στ is [K:E]-to-one onto Hom(E, Q̄_p) and ρ ↦ ρc permutes it. items.name: Discriminant correction to component heights
items.statement: For CM type Φ, h(Φ)−Στ∈Φ h(Φ,τ)=−log(dΦ dΦc)/(4[EΦ:Q]).
proofOutline: Compare determinant of Ω→⊕W with dual map; archimedean map is an isometry; local Vandermonde square equals discriminant. Repair monogenic step by factorwise/unramified descent (E5), whose full descent is a gate.

The E5 repair closes the proof, and the 'full descent is a gate' caveat in the outline is unnecessary. R_Φ is torsion-free over the Dedekind ring O_{E_Φ}, so R_Φ ⊗ O_σ is the image of O_E⊗O_σ = O_σ[t]/P in ∏_{τ∈Φ} K_σ, namely O_σ[t]/P_Φ, and discriminants commute with this flat base change. The proof also uses deg ω(A^t) = deg ω(A), i.e. h(A^t) = h(Φ): A^t has type Φc for the action of p. 544, and h(Φc) = h(Φ). dependsOn should include the missing h(Φ) item (coverage).

items.name: Local Hodge polynomial sequence
items.statement: Let A/K have CM by O_E of type Φ and a good-reduction model 𝒜_σ over O_σ, the completion of O_K at a finite place σ. Assume that K has been enlarged as in the E5 repair, so that O_E ⊗_Z O_σ = O_σ[x] for some x. Let P(t) = ∏_{ρ ∈ Hom(E,K)} (t − x_ρ) ∈ O_σ[t], where x_ρ is the image of x under ρ⊗1 : O_E⊗O_σ → O_σ, and let P_Φ = ∏_{τ∈Φ}(t − x_τ) and P_Φc = ∏_{τ∈Φc}(t − x_τ). Then, with x acting as t, the Hodge–de Rham sequence 0 → Ω(𝒜_σ) → H^1_dR(𝒜_σ/O_σ) → H^1(𝒜_σ, O) → 0 is isomorphic, as a sequence of O_σ⊗O_E-modules, to 0 → O_σ[t]/P_Φ --(·P_Φc)--> O_σ[t]/P → O_σ[t]/P_Φc → 0.
items.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.4, p. 547 (with the E5 repair of the generator x)
proofOutline: Use monicity for exactness, Colmez II.1.2 for rank-one integral de Rham module, and torsion-free type submodules. Not a claim of global Zp-monogeneity.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'On a local factor with monic P' leaves the essential hypothesis implicit: x must generate O_E ⊗_Z O_σ as an O_σ-algebra (possible only after the E5 enlargement of K), and P_Φ, P_Φc must be the products of (t − x_τ) over τ ∈ Φ and Φc. The abelian-scheme data (CM by O_E of type Φ, good-reduction model over O_σ) are also missing. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. With O_E⊗O_σ = O_σ[t]/P (a surjection of free O_σ-modules of rank 2g), the polynomial sequence is exact: injectivity because O_σ[t] is a domain and P = P_Φ P_Φc, and exactness in the middle by Gauss's lemma as printed. Colmez [Col93, Lemma II.1.2] gives H^1_dR ≅ M := O_σ[t]/P. Ω(𝒜_σ) is O_σ-saturated in M and O_E acts on it through Φ, so it lies in M ∩ P_Φc·(M⊗K_σ) = P_Φc·M. Both have rank g and Ω is saturated, so they are equal, and the quotients match. The Colmez input has no item of its own (coverage).

items.name: Totally definite incoherent quaternion datum
items.statement: F totally real of degree g; E/F a CM extension; 𝔹 a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra over A_F: its ramification set Σ(𝔹) has odd cardinality and contains every archimedean place. Fix an A_F-algebra embedding A_E → 𝔹. Let U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 of 𝔹_f containing Ô_E, and let d_𝔹 be the norm of the product of the finite primes of F at which 𝔹 ramifies. Theorems 1.6 and 1.7 assume that no finite place of F ramifies in both E and 𝔹. Theorem 1.7, and §§4–5 as written, also assume |Σ(𝔹)| ≥ 2 (X_U compact, §4.1, p. 561). For an archimedean τ, B = B(τ) is the quaternion algebra over F ramified exactly at Σ(𝔹) ∖ {τ}.
api: fixed embedding, maximal orders, compactness predicate.
unitTests: Nearby real place gives one split archimedean factor.
Exclude the exceptional singleton ramification modular-curve branch when applying compact self-intersection formulas.

The two differ when a place v | 2 of F with residue field F_2 splits in E (new issue). Incoherence (|Σ(𝔹)| odd), the fixed embedding and d_𝔹 should be explicit.

items.name: Two PEL realizations
items.statement: (§3.1) For U′ sufficiently small, X′_{U′} over F′ represents the functor F_{U′} of quadruples [A, ι, θ, κ]: A an abelian scheme up to isogeny, ι : B′ = B⊗_F E → End⁰(A) with tr(ℓ, Lie A) = t(tr_{B′/E} ℓ), where t is the trace of Φ1 + Φ2; θ a polarization whose Rosati involution induces ℓ* = γ′^{-1} ℓ̄ γ′; κ a U′-orbit of B′-skew-hermitian similitudes V̂′ ≅ Ĥ_1(A), for ψ′(v, w) = tr_{E/Q} tr_{B′/E}(γ′ v w̄). Here dim A = 4g. (§3.3, case E ⊂ B) Via B′ ≅ M_2(E) (Morita), X′_{U′} represents the functor F′⁰_{U′} of [A, ι : E → End⁰(A), θ, κ] with tr(ℓ, Lie A) = t(ℓ), a Rosati involution inducing c, and κ : V̂ ≅ Ĥ_1(A) for ψ(u, v) = tr_{F/Q} tr_{B/F}(γ u v̄). Here dim A = 2g. If ψ is integral on Λ = O_B (O_B a maximal order), this is equivalent to the integral functor F′_{U′} with ι : O_E → End(A) and κ : Λ̂ × S → H_1(A, Ẑ).

items.name: Regular small-level PEL models
items.statement: (Case 1: E = F(√λ) with λ a negative integer such that p splits in Q(√λ); ℘′ | p a prime of E over ℘ of F; O_B′,p = O*_B,p ⊕ O_B,p and Λ′_p = O^∨_B,p ⊕ O_B,p.) For U′^p sufficiently small, the moduli problem F_{1,U′^p} is represented by a regular scheme X′_{1,U′^p} over O_(℘′) with the following properties. (1) Via τ′, X′_{1,U′^p}(C) ≅ X′_{U′_p(1)U′^p}(C), where U′_p(1) ≅ Z_p^× × O_B,p^× is the stabilizer of Λ′_p. (2) If ℘ is split in B, X′_{1,U′^p} is smooth over O_℘. (3) If ℘ is ramified in B, X′_{1,U′^p} is a semistable relative Mumford curve: every irreducible component of its special fibre is isomorphic to P^1.
proofOutline: Use special OB℘ Lie condition, étale remaining factors, Carayol moduli and Čerednik uniformization. Original sources remain required.

items.name: Drinfeld-level PEL models are fine moduli
items.statement: (Case 1 of §3.2.) Let n be an ideal of O_F dividing a power of p and prime to d_B. Then the functor F_{n,U′^p} is represented by the minimal regular model X′_{n,U′^p} over O_℘. Over F_{1,U′^p}, F_{n,U′^p} classifies a full level-n structure on the étale part H′^℘_n[n] together with a Drinfeld basis of H′_{n,℘}[n].

items.name: Complex isometric Kodaira–Spencer map
items.statement: (Case 2, U′ small enough that F_{U′} is represented by A_{U′} → X′_{U′}.) Let τ be the place of F missing from Φ1 ∩ Φ2, and set W_{U′} = Ω(A_{U′})_τ and W^t_{U′} = Ω(A^t_{U′})_τ (quotients along x⊗y ↦ τ(x)y). The Hodge filtration 0 → W^t → H^dR_1(A_{U′})_τ → W^∨ → 0 and the Gauss–Manin connection induce an E⊗_F O_{X′}-linear isomorphism W^t → W^∨ ⊗ Ω_{X′}, whose determinant is an isomorphism KS_{U′} : N_{U′} := det W_{U′} ⊗ det W^t_{U′} → Ω^{⊗2}_{X′_{U′}}. At every archimedean place τ′ of F′, KS_{U′} is an isometry when N_{U′} carries the Hodge metric of §2.1 and Ω carries |dz| = 2y (y = Im z) in the complex uniformization.

items.name: Good reduction of PEL CM comparison points
items.statement: (§3.3, case E ⊂ B; U′ sufficiently small that X′_{U′} carries a universal abelian scheme A_{U′}.) Let L be a finite extension of F′ and let x′ ∈ X′_{U′}(L) represent the abelian variety A_{x′} over L. Then A_{x′} has good reduction over O_L. (By Grothendieck and Raynaud it suffices to extend the p-divisible groups locally; that is Proposition 5.2.)
proofOutline: Apply integral extension of the associated p-divisible groups from Proposition5.2 and the good-reduction criterion; do not assume the coarse curve is globally fine moduli.

items.name: Genus at sufficiently small level
items.statement: If U is contained in principal level N≥3, every connected component of the compact quaternionic curve has genus at least 2.
proofOutline: Eliminate noncentral stabilizers by a CM root of unity γ/barγ congruent to 1 modulo N; compact torsion-free upper-half-plane quotient is hyperbolic.

items.name: Quaternionic associated p-divisible tower
items.statement: Let p be a prime and O_{B,p} ⊃ O_{E,p} a maximal order. For an ideal n | p^∞ of O_F put U_p(n) = (1+nO_{B,p})^× and X_n = X/U_p(n), where X = lim X_U carries the action of B_f^× through B_f^×/F̄^×. Since U_p(1) = O_{B,p}^× acts freely on X, H_n := [B_p/O_{B,p} × X]/U_p(n), with U_p(n) acting on B_p/O_{B,p} by right multiplication, is a p-divisible group on X_n. For each n the n-torsion H_1[n] descends to X_{U_p(1)×U^p} as [n^{-1}O_B/O_B × X/(U_p(n)×U^p)]/(U_p(1)/U_p(n)), for every open compact U^p small enough that U_p(1)/U_p(n) acts freely on X/(U_p(n)×U^p). Such U^p exist, as in [Car86, Cor. 1.4.1.3].

Only its finite torsion H_1[n] descends to X_{U_p(1)×U^p} for small U^p. The closure F̄^× of F^× governs the action on X, not the definition of H_n.

items.name: Connected components of the quaternionic and PEL towers
items.statement: There is an isomorphism X^0 ≃ X'^0 of the connected components of the infinite-level quaternionic and PEL curves, compatible with the actions of Δ ≃ Δ'.
proofOutline: As in Carayol [Car86, Prop. 4.2.2]: the embedding G → G'' induces Δ ≃ Δ' and identifies the connected components.

items.name: Small-level quaternionic regular models
items.statement: Fix a prime ℘ | p of O_F. For pairs (n, U^p), with n | p^∞ an ideal of O_F prime to d_B and U^p ⊂ U^p(N) := (1+NÔ_B^p)^× for some N ≥ 3 prime to p, let 𝒳_{n,U^p} be the minimal regular model of X_{U_p(n)U^p}, which exists by Proposition 4.1. Then the schemes 𝒳_{n,U^p} ⊗ O_℘ are regular and form a projective system of curves over O_℘. If ℘ ∤ n, each 𝒳_{n,U^p} ⊗ O_℘ is smooth over O_℘ when ℘ is split in B, and a relative Mumford curve when ℘ is ramified in B.
proofOutline: Transport the PEL connected models through the comparisons and descend along a free quotient.

The proof cites the nonexistent 'Theorem 3.2' (E23). It also uses Proposition 3.5 (level-integral) for the freeness of Ū(N), so it should depend on level-integral too.

items.name: Large-level normal model and rational line descent
items.statement: Let U = ∏_v U_v ⊂ B_f^× be open compact and maximal at every prime ramified in B. Choose a prime p ∤ 2d_B with U_p maximal, and put U′ = U^pU_p(p) with U_p(p) = (1+pO_{B,p})^× and Ū = U/(U∩F̄^×). Define 𝒳_U := 𝒳_{U′}/(Ū/Ū′), the quotient of the minimal regular model 𝒳_{U′} by the finite group Ū/Ū′, whose generic stabilizer is trivial. Then 𝒳_U is a normal integral scheme, projective and flat over O_F. It does not depend on p (Theorem 4.5), and it is the minimal regular model when U ⊂ U(N) for some N ≥ 3. The quotient map π: 𝒳_{U′} → 𝒳_U is finite of degree [Ū:Ū′]; it is flat at codimension-one points, though not necessarily everywhere. The norm N_π(f) = ∏_{u∈Ū/Ū′} u^*f gives, for a line bundle L on 𝒳_{U′}, the line bundle N_π(L), locally generated by symbols N_π(ℓ) subject to N_π(fℓ) = N_π(f)N_π(ℓ). It satisfies N_π(π^*M) = (deg π)·M. The Q-line bundles on S are the objects aL (a ∈ Q), with Isom(aL, bM) := lim_m Isom(L^{⊗am}, M^{⊗bm}); hermitian Q-line bundles are defined analogously.
api: Norm along finite quotient, independence of auxiliary prime, rational Picard groupoid and pullback descent.
unitTests: A regular cover does not assert its coarse quotient regular.
Norm(pullback L)=L^degree in the rational line category.

The construction applies to every U = ∏U_v that is maximal at the B-ramified primes, using an auxiliary prime p ∤ 2d_B with U_p maximal. The statement also omits the degree, the normality, the independence of p, the minimal-regular-model case and the norm identity.

items.name: Q-factoriality after permitted base change
items.statement: After a finite extension H/F unramified at B-ramified and nonmaximal-level places, the model XU,OH is Q-factorial.
proofOutline: Pull Weil divisors to a regular auxiliary cover, make Cartier, descend a multiple by the norm.

Review note: Statement matches Corollary 4.6(2). The first assertion of Corollary 4.6 (the projective system over O_F) and part (1) (smooth or Mumford reduction at small level) are covered by no item; a new item is proposed under coverage. In the proof, 'This proves the case H = K' should read H = F (new misprint). 'By (1)' also needs, at primes where U_℘ is not maximal, that 𝒳_{U′} is regular (being the minimal regular model) and that H is unramified there.

items.name: Arithmetic Hodge Q-line
items.statement: For U ⊂ B_f^× open compact, let L_U ∈ Pic(X_U)_Q be the Hodge bundle of [YZZ13, §3.1.3], L_U = ω_{X_U/F} + Σ_Q (1 − e_Q^{-1})·O(Q), where e_Q is the ramification index of X → X_U at Q. It is compatible with pullback and equals ω_{X_U/F} when Ū acts freely. There is a unique system {L̄_U} of hermitian Q-line bundles on the models 𝒳_U (U = ∏U_v maximal at every prime ramified in B) extending {L_U} such that: (1) the system is invariant under pullback between levels; (2) if U ⊂ U(N) for some N ≥ 3, then for every ℘ with U_℘ maximal there is a canonical isomorphism L_U ⊗ O_℘ = ω_{𝒳_U⊗O_℘/O_℘}, the relative dualizing sheaf; (3) at each archimedean place the metric is ‖dz‖ = 2 Im z under the complex uniformization.
items.locator: §4.2, Theorem 4.7, pp. 567–568 (the generic Hodge bundle is defined on p. 567)
api: distinguish dualizing from naive Kähler differentials at nodes.
unitTests: At a point of ramification e=1 no elliptic correction occurs.
At a nodal fiber use the dualizing line, not an invertible Kähler differential module.

items.name: Integral special formal groups and deformation
items.statement: Let ℘ | p, K = F̂^ur_℘, n | p^∞ an ideal of O_F prime to d_B, and 𝒳_n the projective limit over U^p of 𝒳_{U_p(n)U^p} ⊗ O_K. Then H_n has an integral model ℋ_n over 𝒳_n such that: (1) with H = H_℘ × H^℘ according to O_{F,p} = O_℘ ⊕ O^℘_{F,p}, ℋ^℘ is étale over 𝒳_1 and ℋ_℘ is a special formal O_{B,℘}-module, i.e. Lie(ℋ_℘) is locally free of rank 1 over O_{𝒳_1} ⊗_{O_℘} O_{K_0} for an unramified quadratic extension K_0 ⊂ B_℘ of F_℘; (2) the formal completion 𝒳̂_1 along its special fibre over k̄ (k = O_F/℘) is the universal deformation space of ℋ_{k̄}; (3) for n = ℘^m·n′ with n′ prime to ℘, 𝒳_n → 𝒳_1 classifies pairs consisting of a full level-n′ structure on ℋ^℘_1 and a Drinfeld level-℘^m structure on ℋ_{1,℘}.
proofOutline: Transport integral PEL groups using Carayol comparisons and deformation representability; original moduli proofs remain a gate.

Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'Extends uniquely over the small-level model' is imprecise. The base is 𝒳_n, the limit over U^p of 𝒳_{U_p(n)U^p} ⊗ O_K (n prime to d_B), and the paper asserts the existence of an integral model with properties (1)–(3), not uniqueness. The Drinfeld-level clause should be stated. Review note: Partly planned by R18.2 (Carayol integral models). The proof cites the nonexistent 'Theorem 3.5' (new misprint; read Proposition 3.5, with Proposition 3.2 and the description of H′ on pp. 555–556).

items.name: Integral Kodaira–Spencer discriminant twist
items.statement: Let ℘ | p, K = F̂^ur_℘, and 𝒳_℘ the tower of regular models 𝒳_{1,U^p} ⊗ O_K (Theorem 4.5), with the special formal O_{B,℘}-module ℋ_℘ (Theorem 4.9). Let M_℘ be its O_℘-relative covariant Dieudonné crystal (for F_℘/Q_p unramified, the τ-part of the absolute crystal), with Hodge filtration 0 → W^t_℘ → M_℘ → W_℘^∨ → 0, where W_℘ = Lie(ℋ_℘)^∨ and W^t_℘ = Lie(ℋ^t_℘)^∨ both have rank 2. Put N_℘ := det W^t_℘ ⊗ det W_℘ (E8), and let KS_℘: N_℘ → ω^{⊗2} be induced by W^t_℘ → M_℘ →(∇) M_℘ ⊗ ω → W_℘^∨ ⊗ ω, where ω is the relative dualizing sheaf of 𝒳_℘/O_K. Let d_{B,℘} = ℘ if B_℘ is a division algebra and 0 otherwise. Then KS_℘ extends to an isomorphism N_℘ ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−d_{B,℘}).
items.locator: Theorem4.10 pp569–570, corrected determinant convention E8
proofOutline: Split case uses matrix idempotents/Morita; division case uses the two eigenspaces and j²=π. The printed unit argument at nodes is not sufficient (E9); establish on the smooth locus and extend across codimension two on the regular model if justified.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item should name the base and the objects. X_℘ is the tower of regular models 𝒳_{1,U^p} ⊗ O_K at maximal level at ℘ (K = F̂^ur_℘), not a 'small-level' model at ℘. For [F_℘:Q_p] > 1, W_℘ and W^t_℘ must be the rank-2 τ-parts, or the O_℘-relative Dieudonné objects of the strict module ℋ_℘; the absolute Lie(ℋ^t_℘)^∨ has rank 4[F_℘:Q_p] − 2 (new issue). Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The E8 convention N_℘ = det W^t ⊗ det W is forced by the construction: taking determinants of W^t → W^∨ ⊗ ω gives det W^t → (det W)^{-1} ⊗ ω^{⊗2}, that is, det W^t ⊗ det W → ω^{⊗2}. It is also what the split-case line on p. 569 computes, ω^{-2} ≅ (det W^t)^∨ ⊗ (det W)^∨, and it matches Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 5.5. With it, the division-case computation gives ω^{-2} = πN^∨, i.e. N = πω^2 = ω^{⊗2}(−d_{B,℘}). The E9 repair in the proof outline is valid, not merely 'if justified'. Off the nodes, π is a prime local equation of the reduced special fibre, so exactly one of j1, j2 is a unit and the printed computation applies. The nodes are closed points, of codimension 2, of the regular finite-level models 𝒳_{1,U^p} ⊗ O_K, and a map of line bundles on a normal scheme that is an isomorphism off codimension 2 is an isomorphism. Caveats: (i) the extraction's E9 correction writes π^{-1}N^∨ where πN^∨ is meant; (ii) the rank caveat for [F_℘:Q_p] > 1 (new issue at p. 569); (iii) the proof also contains misprints: Ω(H_0) for Ω(H_℘), and 'nonsplit in F' for 'nonsplit in B' (new misprint). Status missing is right; R18.2 and R18.5 plan the models and the Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, not this isomorphism.

items.name: Torus bridge and contracted product curve
items.statement: Let (Φ1,Φ2) be a nearby pair, Ψ = Φ1∩Φ2, F′ the reflex field of Φ1+Φ2, τ′ | τ an archimedean place of F′, and B the quaternion algebra over F ramified at Σ(𝔹)∖{τ}. Put G″ = B^× ×_{F^×} E^×, so that G″(A_f) = 𝔹_f^× ×_{A_f^×} A_{E,f}^×. Give it the Hodge structure h″ induced from h′ via G′ → G″; its reflex field is F′. Then X″ = lim X″_U, with X″_{U,τ′}(C) = G″(Q)∖h^± × G″(Q̂)/U, is a system of Shimura curves over F′ on which Z″ = {(1,x) : x ∈ Ē^×} acts trivially, and G′ → G″ embeds X′ in X″. Let Y = lim Y_J be the zero-dimensional Shimura variety over F′ of E^× with h_Ψ: z ↦ (1, z^{-1}, …, z^{-1}) through Φ1, the entry 1 sitting at the element of Φ1∖Φ2; its geometric points form a principal homogeneous space over Ē^×∖Ê^×. The morphism B^× × E^× → G″ gives f: X ×_F Y → X″, compatible with the group actions, and an isomorphism (X ×_F Y)/Δ(F̂^×) ≅ X″, where Δ(z) = (z, z^{-1}). With X″_1 = X″/U″_p(1) and Y_1 = Y/O^×_{E,p}, it induces f_1: (X_1 ×_F Y_1)/Δ(F̂^×) ≅ X″_1. Define H″ = (B_p/O_{B,p} × X″)/U″_p(1) and I = (E_p/O_{E,p} × Y)/O^×_{E,p}, with x·(b,e) = exb and y·e = ey. Both descend to finite level as in [Car86, Cor. 1.4.1.3], and H′ = H″|X′.
api: Descent action (z,z^−1), torus reciprocity, finite components and associated Tate modules.
unitTests: The torus quotient uses the closure of global E*.
Ramified base change of a Mumford model need not remain regular.

It also omits the p-divisible group H″ and the level-one quotients X″_1, Y_1 with the isomorphism f_1. H″ is used by Propositions 5.1–5.4 and is covered by no item.

items.name: Tensor identity for Tate sheaves
items.statement: On X×Y, the pullback of T_pH'' is T_pH⊗OE,p T_pI.
proofOutline: Write associated sheaves from the common contracted-product action; check equivariance before descending.

items.name: Integral extension at comparison points
items.statement: Let L be a finite extension of K′ = F̂′^ur_℘′. For every y ∈ Y(L), x′ ∈ X′(L) and x″ ∈ X″(L), the p-divisible groups I_y, H′_{x′} and H″_{x″} over L extend uniquely to p-divisible groups over O_L. The proof: T(I) is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in {0,−1}. For x″ the image of (x,y) ∈ (X_1×Y_1)(L), Proposition 5.1 gives T(H″_{x″}) ≅ T(H_x) ⊗_{O_{E,p}} T(I_y), which is crystalline with weights in {0,−1}. The extension then follows from Breuil–Kisin [Kis06] for p > 2 and from Kim, Lau and Liu for p = 2, and uniqueness from Tate's theorem.
proofOutline: Use crystalline Tate modules with HT weights {0,−1} and Kisin existence/uniqueness; verify the complementary CM components before tensoring, since arbitrary tensor products may have weight −2.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement ('for the fields and points in §5.2') should be explicit. The printed proof cites [Kis06], which assumes p > 2; for p = 2 one needs Kim/Lau/Liu (new gap). The weight check that the item's outline asks for does hold: at embeddings above τ, I has weight 0; above τ′ ≠ τ, ℋ_℘ has weight 0 because it is strict; and ℋ^℘ is étale. Review note: missing. The Breuil–Kisin input (a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in {0,1} comes from a Barsotti–Tate group, the dyadic case included) is what FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 plans.

items.name: Integral filtered Dieudonné tensor comparison
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 5.2, let (x,y) ∈ (X_1×Y_1)(L) map to x″, with ℋ″_{x″}, ℋ_x and ℐ_y the extensions over O_L. There is a canonical isomorphism of filtered O_{E,p} ⊗ O_L-modules D(ℋ″_{x″}) ≃ D(ℋ_x) ⊗_{O_{E,p}⊗O_L} D(ℐ_y), where each D(G) carries 0 → Ω(G^t) → D(G) → Ω(G)^∨ → 0. It is obtained from Proposition 5.1 through Kisin's tensor-compatible functor M on integral crystalline representations and D(G) = O_L ⊗_𝔖 φ^*M(T(G)) ([Kis10, Th. 1.4.2] for p ≠ 2; Kim, Lau and Liu for p = 2).
proofOutline: Use integral Kisin tensor functor with filtration compatibility and dyadic Kim/Lau/Liu inputs. Rational comparison alone is insufficient.

The filtration on the tensor product has to be the one given by Kisin's formula; with the covariant convention, Fil = Ω(G^t) and the τ-part of I is of étale type. items.name: Cotangent cancellation under the torus tensor
items.statement: Let L ⊃ K′ be finite, (x,y) ∈ (X_1×Y_1)(L) with image x″, W(−) the τ-quotients for τ: O_{F,p} ⊗_{Z_p} O_L → O_L, and O_{E,L} = O_{E,℘} ⊗_{O_℘} O_L. If F_℘/Q_p is unramified, then W(I_y) = 0 and W(I^t_y) is free of rank 1 over O_{E,L}, and there are canonical isomorphisms W(ℋ″^t_{x″}) ≃ W(ℋ^t_x) ⊗_{O_{E,L}} W(ℐ^t_y) and W(ℋ″_{x″}) ≃ W(ℋ_x) ⊗_{O_{E,L}} W(ℐ^t_y)^∨. When F_℘/Q_p is ramified, W(I_y) is a nonzero torsion module, the τ-quotient sequences need not be left exact, and the isomorphisms need an integral argument that the paper does not give.
proofOutline: Extract the Hodge terms from the filtered tensor comparison of Proposition 5.3.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'W(I_y) = 0' is false integrally when e(F_℘/Q_p) > 1 (new error at p. 575). With W(−) the τ-quotient for O_{F,p} ⊗ O_L → O_L, the τ′-components of Ω(I_y) (τ′ ≠ τ, same residue embedding) leave a nonzero torsion module O_L/(τ′(x) − τ(x) : x ∈ O_℘). So the displayed isomorphisms are proved only when F_℘/Q_p is unramified. The ring is O_L (L ⊃ K′), not O_K.

items.name: Compatible CM point across X,X',X''
items.statement: Let y ∈ Y be a fixed point, P ∈ X the fixed CM point of T(Q) = E^×, and P″ ∈ X″ the image of (P,y); P″ is fixed by T″(Q). Then there is an embedding X′ → X″, induced by G′ → G″, such that P″ is the image of a point P′ ∈ X′ fixed by T′(Q). The CM points P_U, P′_{U′} and P″_{U″} at the maximal levels defined by the maximal order O_B ⊃ Ô_E are then compatible under X_U → X″_{U″} ← X′_{U′}.
proofOutline: Use Shimura reciprocity and adelic descriptions of components, not an arbitrary equality of complex points.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. The lemma asserts the existence of an embedding X′ → X″ carrying a T′(Q)-fixed point onto P″.

items.name: Isometric comparison of CM determinant lines
items.statement: Let A0 be the abelian variety with O_E-action represented by P′_{U′}, defined over a finite extension K of F′(P′_{U′}) containing F(P_U) over which it has good reduction. Let N̄_U := L̄_U^{⊗2}(−d_B). Then N̄(A0,τ) ≃ N̄_{P_U} ⊗_{O_{F(P_U)}} O_K as hermitian line bundles over O_K. Here N̄(A0,τ) = det W(A0,τ) ⊗ det W(A0^t,τ) is formed with the O_F-action at the distinguished place τ of F, and N̄_{P_U} is the restriction of N̄_U to the closure of P_U.
proofOutline: Combine complex KS with local filtered tensor cancellation at every finite place; use good reduction of A0.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Imprecise ('over the required common field'). The line N(A0,τ) is formed with the O_F-action, which is the version Theorem 1 of the erratum supplies.

items.name: Graph-of-different-torsion isogeny
items.statement: For nearby CM types Φi and K/Q finite Galois containing E, take OE-abelian varieties A,A1,A2 with good reduction over OK, Ai of type Φi, and an OE-isogeny A1×A2→A whose kernel is the graph of an OE-isomorphism A1[δE/F]≃A2[δE/F].
items.locator: Erratum, §1, Theorem 1, hypotheses (1)–(2), p. 2 (K is a finite extension of E in C, Galois over Q, p. 1)
api: graph subgroup with both projections isomorphisms
unitTests: At an E/F-unramified place δ is a unit and its torsion vanishes.
No replacement by an arbitrary OE-isogeny, or by the earlier arXiv kernel-support condition.

items.name: Corrected nearby-isogeny identity
items.statement: For the preceding graph-kernel datum, h(Φ1,Φ2)=(h(A1,τ1)+h(A2,τ2))/2=h(A,τ)/2, where τ is the common place of F and A in the last expression is viewed with OF action.
items.locator: Erratum, §1, Theorem 1, p. 2; proof in Erratum §3, pp. 9–11 (Proposition 6 and Theorem 2)
proofOutline: Extend the generic graph isomorphism on different torsion locally, identify the integral kernel, prove conjugation-trivial self-duality, and apply the differential-length height criterion.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement is Erratum Theorem 1 verbatim. The reduction checks. Proposition 6, applied to f̃ : A1 × A2 → A at both embeddings τ1 and τ2 of E over τ, gives h(A,τ1) + h(A,τ2) = h(A1,τ1) + h(A2,τ2): h(A2,τ1) = h(A1,τ2) = 0, and N(A,τ_F) = N(A,τ1) ⊗ N(A,τ2) isometrically. Its hypotheses hold: the kernel over Ŏ_σ is the flat closure of the generic graph, hence the graph of the lift ν given by Theorem 2; self-duality comes from Q^t ≅ A1^t[δ] ≅ A1[δ] ≅ Q; and conjugation is trivial on O_E/δ_{E/F}, because x − x̄ ∈ δ_{E/F} for all x ∈ O_E. The replacement suffices for the paper. Corollary 2.6 never uses Theorem 2.7. Theorem 1.6 uses it once, at p. 577, for A0 at P′_{U′} = [z0, 1], which Erratum §1 verifies (see quaternion-graph-kernel).

items.name: The actual quaternionic isogeny meets the repaired hypothesis
items.statement: Let B = B(τ) ⊃ E with B = E + Ej, where jx = x̄j, and let O_B be a maximal order of B containing O_E. Assume that no finite place of F ramifies in both E and B. Set Λ1 = O_E, Λ2 = Ej ∩ O_B and Λ0 = O_B. Give V1 = E⊗R and V2 = Ej⊗R complex structures for which left multiplication by E has types Φ1 and Φ2, and let A_i = V_i/Λ_i, with A0 = (V1 ⊕ V2)/Λ0. Then f : A1 × A2 → A0 has kernel Λ0/(Λ1 + Λ2), and both projections Ker f → A_i are injective with image A_i[δ_{E/F}] = δ^{-1}Λ_i/Λ_i. So Ker f is the graph of an O_E-isomorphism A1[δ_{E/F}] ≅ A2[δ_{E/F}]. Locally the kernel is 0 at B-ramified ℘, and at B-split ℘ it is generated by (ϖ − ϖ̄)^{-1}(1 − j_℘).
items.locator: Erratum, §1, pp. 2–3 (Vignéras citation: [Vi, Ch. II, Théorème 3.2, p. 44])
proofOutline: At B-ramified primes the lattice splits and kernel is zero. At B-split primes identify OB with EndOF(OE); solve a+b=x, aϖ+b barϖ=y to get δ^−1(1−j) and graph projections. Requires integral conjugacy of maximal quadratic embeddings (Vignéras III.3.2).
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Two points. (a) The statement needs O_E ⊂ O_B: the erratum takes Λ1 = O_E ⊂ Λ0 = O_B, and p. 576 fixes O_𝔹 ⊇ Ô_E, but 'U maximal ⊇ Ô_E^×' does not imply it (new issue). (b) The outline's citation 'Vignéras III.3.2' is wrong. The erratum cites [Vi, Theorem 3.2, p. 44], and p. 44 of LNM 800 lies in Chapter II, the local theory (pp. 31–56; Chapter III is pp. 57–102). Review note: Argument rechecked. At B-ramified ℘, E_℘ is an unramified field by hypothesis, so O_B,℘ = O_E,℘ + O_E,℘ j_℘ with q(j_℘) of valuation 1, Λ0 = Λ1 + Λ2 and δ is a unit there. At B-split ℘, a + b = x and aϖ + bϖ̄ = y give Λ0 = O_E j_℘ + (ϖ − ϖ̄)^{-1}O_E(1 − j_℘) and Λ2 = O_E j_℘; the element a·(ϖ − ϖ̄)^{-1}(1 − j_℘) maps to (au, −au j_℘) with u = (ϖ − ϖ̄)^{-1}, so both projections are O_E/δ-isomorphisms onto δ^{-1}Λ_i/Λ_i. Translating by t ∈ T̂′ (x ↦ exb acts by eb on E and eb̄ on Ej) preserves the graph property, so it holds at every point of X′^{T′}.

items.name: Formal CM p-divisible type
items.statement: Let w | v be a place of E ramified over the place v | p of F, and σ a place of K over p with K_σ containing the Galois closure of E_w. A local CM type is a subset Θ ⊂ Hom_{Q_p}(E_w, K_σ) containing exactly one element of each pair {θ, θ∘c}. Over Ŏ_σ there is, up to O_w-isomorphism, exactly one p-divisible group Ğ_Θ of height [E_w:Q_p] with an O_w-action whose Lie algebra has type Θ [CCO, Prop. 3.7.4(1)], and it is formal (isoclinic of slope 1/2). If 𝒜/O_K has CM by O_E of type Φ, then 𝒜[w^∞]_{Ŏσ} ≅ Ğ_Θ, where Θ is the preimage of Φ under Hom(E_w, K_σ) → Hom(E, K_σ) ≅ Hom(E, K).
items.locator: Erratum, §2 (proof of Theorem 2), p. 4; the model G_Θ over O_σ is constructed in Proposition 4, p. 7. The erratum has no numbered subsections §2.1–§2.4.
api: Height [Ew:Qp], CM Lie condition, uniqueness over the strictly unramified complete base, conjugate dual type.
unitTests: Different choices Θ,Θ' need not give isomorphic full p-divisible groups.
Their different-torsion may nonetheless be isomorphic.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Existence and uniqueness belong over Ŏ_σ. Over O_σ, CM p-divisible groups of a given type are unique only up to unramified twist. The erratum takes Ğ_Θ := 𝒜[w^∞]_{Ŏσ} and builds the model G_Θ = G(𝔐_Θ) over O_σ in Proposition 4.

items.name: Nilpotent height-one Kisin module
items.statement: Let Sfrak=W(k)[[u]], φ Witt Frobenius with u↦u^p, and Eis(u) the Eisenstein polynomial of the chosen uniformizer. A finite free module M has φ-semilinear map with linearized cokernel killed by Eis and ψ with φ_lin ψ=Eis; the formal-group subcategory requires the stated topological nilpotence of ψ.
api: Linearization φ*M, height-one cokernel, ψ, morphisms commuting with φ, nilpotence and base change.
unitTests: Height one is an Eisenstein annihilation condition, not invertibility over Sfrak.
Retain the formal/connected restriction at p=2.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Looks planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 plans the power-series ring, Frobenius modules with the Eisenstein height bound, and the classification including the dyadic theorem. The status could be 'planned: R07.4'. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): status changed from missing to planned (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4). R07.4 plans the power-series coefficient ring, the Frobenius modules and the height bound given by the Eisenstein polynomial. This paper's normalizations remain the source for that layer, and the item stays in its source route.

items.name: Formal p-divisible/Kisin classification input
items.statement: Let O_σ be a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k and uniformizer π, W = W(k), Eis(u) ∈ W[u] the Eisenstein polynomial of π, 𝔖 = W[[u]] → O_σ (u ↦ π), φ(u) = u^p, and S the p-adic completion of W[u, Eis(u)^n/n!] with Fil^1S = ker(S → O_σ). [Ki09, Th. 1.2.8]: 𝔐 ↦ G(𝔐) is an exact equivalence from BT^{φ,f}_{/𝔖} (as in kisin-free) to formal p-divisible groups over O_σ, for every p including p = 2. It is characterized by D(G(𝔐))(S) = S ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔐, an identity of S-windows, where D is the covariant Dieudonné crystal. [Ki10, Th. 1.2.1(1)]: the Hodge filtration is Fil^1(S ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔐) = {y : (1⊗φ)(y) ∈ Fil^1S ⊗_𝔖 𝔐}.
items.locator: Erratum, §2, p. 5, displays (1)–(3), citing [Ki09, Theorem 1.2.8, p. 599] and [Ki10, Theorem 1.2.1(1), p. 974]
proofOutline: External theorem: acquire Kisin's original hypotheses, variance, nilpotence and integral comparison. This item is a verified citation contract, not a locally closed proof.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement omits the two inputs that Lemma 3 uses. One is the window identity D(G(𝔐))(S) = S ⊗_{𝔖,φ} 𝔐, which characterizes the functor; the other is the Hodge filtration formula (3) from [Ki10, Th. 1.2.1(1)]. Review note: Looks planned by FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 (classification of p-divisible groups, including the dyadic theorem). The variance convention does not matter for Theorem 2: Proposition 5 is symmetric in Θ, so a contravariant convention would only swap Θ and Θ̄. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): status changed from missing to planned (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4). R07.4 plans the classification of finite flat groups and p-divisible groups by Breuil–Kisin modules, including the dyadic theorem. This paper's normalizations remain the source for that layer, and the item stays in its source route.

items.name: Lie module from the Kisin window
items.statement: For the formal p-divisible group attached to M in the chosen covariant convention, Lie(G)≃φ*M/ψ(M).
proofOutline: Use the Dieudonné display/window and its Hodge filtration; compute the image of linearized Frobenius modulo Eis. Match Ki10 convention before exporting.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Proof checked and correct. D/Fil^1 is the image of 1⊗φ in (S/Fil^1S) ⊗ 𝔐 = O_σ ⊗ 𝔐. Since S = Fil^1S + 𝔖 and 1⊗φ is injective, this image is φ^*𝔐/ψ(𝔐).

items.name: Explicit CM-type Kisin module
items.statement: Decompose Sfrak⊗Zp Ow over residue embeddings ι as ⊕ι Oι[[u]]eι. Factor Eis into CM embedding factors Eisθ, set EisΘ,ι=∏θ∈Θι Eisθ, and give φ,ψ coefficients EisbarΘ,ι and EisΘ,ι with the Frobenius permutation of components.
api: verify product Eis, height and nilpotence
unitTests: Θ and its complement multiply to the full Eisenstein factor.
Indices move under Frobenius; never use componentwise scalar maps without that permutation.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The item rightly insists on the Frobenius permutation. The printed semilinear formula φ_Θ(e_ι) = Eis_{Θ̄ι}(u)e_ι, and ψ_n with a fixed ι, are misprints when k_v ≠ F_p (new issue). The linearized formula (1⊗φ_Θ)(ẽ_ι) = Eis_{Θ̄ι}(u)e_ι is correct and is the one used. Checked: Eis(u) = ∏_θ Eis_θ(u) = Eis_{Θι}·Eis_{Θ̄ι} in O_ι[u], because K_σ/K_0 is Galois and π is a simple root.

items.name: Explicit module realizes the CM group
items.statement: 𝔐_Θ with φ_Θ lies in BT^{φ,f}_{/𝔖}: ψ(e_ι) = Eis_{Θ_ι}(u)ẽ_ι, and ψ_n lands in (p,u)φ^{n*}𝔐_Θ for n ≥ 2. G(𝔐_Θ) has height [O_w:Z_p] and an O_w-action, and Lie(G(𝔐_Θ)) ≅ ⊕_ι (O_σ ⊗_{W(k_v),ι} O_w)/Eis_{Θ_ι}(π) has type Θ. Hence G(𝔐_Θ) ⊗ Ŏ_σ ≅ Ğ_Θ [CCO, Prop. 3.7.4(1)].
proofOutline: Compute Lie through Lemma3, identify θ-eigenspaces, prove topological nilpotence from uniformizer factors and invoke CCO3.7.4.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'Hence is isomorphic to G_Θ by uniqueness' holds over Ŏ_σ only. Over O_σ, CM groups of a given type are unique only up to unramified twist. The nilpotence bound is also misprinted: n ≥ [O_v : W(k_v)] fails when F_v/Q_p is unramified, and n ≥ 2 is what is needed (new misprint). Review note: Type computation checked. For λ ∈ Hom_W(O_ι, K_σ), λ(Eis_θ)(π) = 0 iff θ = λ, because π is a simple root of Eis = ∏_θ λ(Eis_θ). The constant term of Eis_{Θι} is ϖ^{e_v}·unit with p = ϖ^{2e_v}·unit, so the constant term of ψ_n is ϖ^{n·e_v}·unit, and n ≥ 2 is needed.

items.name: Torsion Kisin module and different quotient
items.statement: Use p-power-torsion, projective-dimension-one Kisin modules with height-one and connected/nilpotent conditions. MΘ/δw is the module of GΘ[δw], with the variance fixed by its presentation.
api: Ow-linear Cartier dual and generic fiber.
unitTests: Do not replace torsion objects by finite free modules.
δ a unit gives the zero torsion module.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The classification theorem behind 'M_Θ/δ_w is the module of G_Θ[δ_w]' is [Ki09, Th. 1.3.9], an equivalence from (Mod/𝔖)^c to connected finite flat group schemes, together with its compatibility with isogenies. No item states it, so a new coverage item is proposed; R07.4 looks like its planned owner. G_Θ[δ_w] is connected because G_Θ is formal.

items.name: CM-type independence modulo the different
items.statement: For ramified quadratic Ew/Fv, the Ow-linear torsion Kisin modules MΘ/δw are independent of Θ, since coefficients of conjugate embedding polynomials agree modulo δw.
proofOutline: Use x−bar x∈δw and factor comparisons to identify φ and ψ after reduction. Classification then yields an integral group-scheme isomorphism.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Proof checked and correct. Eis_{θ̄} = c(Eis_θ) because θ∘c(K_ι) = θ(K_ι), and the ideal of O_ι generated by the x − x̄ is δ_wO_ι, since O_w = O_v[ϖ] and δ_w = (ϖ − ϖ̄). So the linearized Frobenius of 𝔐_Θ/δ_w is independent of Θ, and the identity map is an O_w-linear isomorphism.

items.name: Extension of every different-torsion isomorphism
items.statement: For abelian schemes A,A' over OK with CM by OE (types may differ), and every finite σ of K, IsomOE(A[δ]Ocheckσ,A'[δ]Ocheckσ)→IsomOE(A[δ]Kcheckσ,A'[δ]Kcheckσ) is bijective.
proofOutline: Different residue characteristics give finite étale constant groups. At matching characteristic use local CM groups, explicit Kisin quotients and the rank-one Hom description; transport all generic isomorphisms, not just existence of one.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Statement correct. §2 of the erratum proves only that Ğ_Θ[δ_w] ≅ Ğ_Θ′[δ_w], that is, that some integral isomorphism exists. The asserted bijection of Isom sets needs one more step, the extension of O_E-linear automorphisms (new gap, easily filled). §3 re-derives what it needs by counting Homs over O_w/δ_w. The reduction to places w of the same residue characteristic is correct: the other factors are étale, hence constant over Ŏ_σ. Theorem 2 is applied in §3 both to (A1, A2) and to (A1^t, A1), so K must be enlarged until the A_i^t[δ] are constant as well.

items.name: Local self-dual kernel height invariance
items.statement: Let f: 𝒳 → 𝒴 be an O_E-isogeny of abelian schemes over O_K. Suppose that for every finite place σ the kernel 𝒬 satisfies (1) 𝒬_{Ŏσ} ≅ 𝒬^t_{Ŏσ} as O_E-module schemes, with the dual action on 𝒬^t, and (2) O_E → End(𝒬_{Ŏσ}) is invariant under complex conjugation. Let o be O_E or O_F, and let τ be an embedding of Frac(o) into K. Suppose further that the τ-quotients (for o) of Ω(𝒳), Ω(𝒴), Ω(𝒳^t) and Ω(𝒴^t), the last two at τ^c, are locally free O_K-modules. Then h(X,τ) = h(Y,τ). For o = O_F this holds at every σ over a prime unramified in F, and that is the case Theorem 1 needs. Elsewhere a determinant convention for τ-quotients with torsion must be fixed, compatibly with §2.2 of the paper, and the length count redone.
proofOutline: Take invariant-differential exact sequences; the determinant order is length Ω(Q,τ)−length Ω(Q^t,τc), which vanishes by the two separate hypotheses. Equal torsion-free ranks suffice; rank need not be two.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: As printed, the proposition is stated for every τ: E → K, but its proof asserts that Ω(X,τ) and Ω(Y,τ) are 'locally free of rank 2'. That claim is false in general (E3). The ranks are the multiplicities of τ, and the τ-quotients can have torsion when E/F, or F/Q for the O_F version, is ramified at σ. Theorem 1 uses the O_F version, where the rank is 2. The item's outline ('equal torsion-free ranks suffice') misses the torsion. Review note: missing. The isogeny variation is ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.4; the identification ker(f^t) = 𝒬^D is an extra input (new coverage item).

items.name: CM average to quaternionic Hodge height
items.statement: Let E/F, 𝔹 and A_E → 𝔹 be as in §1.2. Assume at least two places of F ramify in 𝔹 (X_U compact) and no finite place of F ramifies in both E and 𝔹. Let U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 ⊇ Ô_E, let P_U be the image in X_U of a CM point P ∈ X^{E^×}, and let d_𝔹 be the norm of the product of the finite primes where 𝔹 ramifies. Then 2^{-g} Σ_Φ h(Φ) = ½ h_{L̄_U}(P_U) − ¼ log(d_𝔹 d_F), with Φ over all 2^g CM types of E and h the Faltings height normalized as on p. 534.
items.locator: §1.2, Theorem 1.6, p. 537; proof §5.3, pp. 576–577, with Theorem 2.7 replaced by Erratum §1, Theorem 1 (p. 2) and its verification on pp. 2–3
proofOutline: Apply the repaired nearby identity only to the actual quaternionic graph kernel; use the isometric comparison line and N_U=L_U²(−dB); average the nearby pairs.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: (a) The U hypothesis must be U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 of 𝔹_f containing Ô_E (the order actually fixed on p. 576 and used on p. 591); 'U maximal compact containing Ô_E^×' alone is weaker when a place v | 2 of F with residue field F_2 splits in E (new issue below). (b) 'Compact' is not in the printed Theorem 1.6. It is justified: Part I is proved only for compact X_U (§4.1, p. 561), and the paper's unrestricted claim is a gap (new issue). (c) The item should name P_U as the image of P ∈ X^{E^×}, with h_{L_U} the Hodge height of p. 537. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound, under the corrected U hypothesis (with the literal 'maximal U ⊇ Ô_E^×' it is unproved in the dyadic F_2-split case). The chain in the outline is correct and complete, and the arithmetic checks. Corollary 2.6 gives 2^{-g}Σh(Φ) = 2^{1−g}Σ_unordered h(Φ1,Φ2) − ¼ log d_F. For each of the g·2^{g−1} unordered pairs, Erratum Theorem 1 with the §1 verification gives h(Φ1,Φ2) = ½h(A0,τ). Proposition 5.7, an isometry N(A0,τ) ≅ N_{P_U} ⊗ O_K with N_U = L_U²(−d_𝔹), gives h(A0,τ) = (1/(2[F:Q]))(2h_L(P_U) − log d_𝔹). Hence g·h(Φ1,Φ2) = ½h_L(P_U) − ¼ log d_𝔹, and the sum is ½h_L(P_U) − ¼ log(d_𝔹 d_F). The graph verification needs O_E ⊂ O_B and the no-common-ramification hypothesis, both carried. dependsOn should also list the CM-point height definition, which has no item (coverage).

items.name: Quadratic Hecke L-function conventions
items.statement: For the quadratic CM character η of E/F, distinguish finite Lf(s,η) from L(s,η)=Lf(s,η)Γ_R(s+1)^g. Use absolute discriminants dE,dF and relative discriminant norm dE/F with dE=dF²dE/F; keep local additive-character differents dv.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 535 (L_f(s,η) is the finite part of the completed L(s,η)); §7.1, p. 590 (L_∞(s,η) = (π^{−(s+1)/2}Γ((s+1)/2))^m, m = [F:Q])
api: Euler factors, completed functional equation, nonzero Lf(0,η), logarithmic derivative and discriminant conversion.
unitTests: For F=Q there is one shifted real gamma factor.
Relative discriminant norm is not the absolute discriminant dE.
items.note: Review note: planned AL.1 (Tate zeta integrals of Hecke quasi-characters, real/complex gamma factors, global functional equation): covers L(s,η). The finite/archimedean split and d_E = d_F²·d_{E/F} (used as log|d_E/d_F| on p. 590) should be recorded there.

items.name: Extended Schwartz space and Weil action
items.statement: For even-dimensional positive definite V/F, use S(V(A)×A*): finite factors are locally constant compactly supported functions; real factors have form (P1(uq(x))+sgn(u)P2(uq(x)))exp(−2π|u|q(x)). The standard real function is exp(−2πu q(x))1_(u>0). Use the extended GL2(A)×GO(V)(A) Weil action.
items.locator: §6.1, p. 578 (from [YZZ13, §§2.1.3, 4.1] and [Wal85]; the space is YZZ's S̄(V(A)×A^×))
api: Restricted tensor product, action formulas, standard Gaussian, similitude scaling of x,u and self-dual measure.

Do not identify nonarchimedean Schwartz–Bruhat functions with real SchwartzMap.

items.name: Theta convergence and automorphy
items.statement: Let F be totally real, (V,q) a positive definite even-dimensional quadratic space over F, φ ∈ S̄(V(A)×A^×), K ⊂ GO(V(A_f)) an open compact subgroup fixing φ_f under the Weil representation, and µ_K = F^×∩K. Then θ(g,φ)_K = Σ_{u∈µ_K²\F^×} Σ_{x∈V} r(g)φ(x,u) is well defined and absolutely convergent and is an automorphic form in g ∈ GL2(A); θ(g,r(h)φ)_K is an automorphic form in (g,h) ∈ GL2(A)×GO(V(A)); and if φ_∞ is the standard Gaussian, θ(g,φ)_K is holomorphic of parallel weight (1/2)dim V.
proofOutline: Adelic Poisson summation and μ-quotient convergence; keep the extended action and archimedean weight conventions.

items.name: Pseudo-theta datum
items.statement: Let V be a positive definite quadratic space over F and V0 ⊂ V1 ⊂ V subspaces over F with the induced forms, all even-dimensional; V0 may also be ∅. Let S be a finite set of nonarchimedean places, φ^S ∈ S̄(V(A^S)×A^{S,×}) with standard archimedean components, and for v ∈ S let φ′_v : GL2(F_v)×(V1−V0)(F_v)×F_v^× → ℂ be locally constant, invariant under right translation of g by some open compact K_v ⊂ GL2(F_v), and, for each g, of bounded support in (x,u); let µ ⊂ O_F^× have finite index with φ^S and φ′_S = ∏_{v∈S}φ′_v invariant under (x,u) ↦ (αx, α^{−2}u), α ∈ µ. The pseudo-theta series is A^{(S)}_{φ′}(g) = Σ_{u∈µ²\F^×} Σ_{x∈V1−V0} φ′_S(g,x,u) r_V(g)φ^S(x,u), with the Weil representation of V (not V1). It is nondegenerate if V1 = V, nontruncated if V0 = ∅, and nonsingular if each φ′_v(1,·,·) extends to a Schwartz function on V1(F_v)×F_v^×; then its outer theta series is θ_{A,1}(g) = Σ_u Σ_{x∈V1} r_{V1}(g)φ′_S(1,x,u) r_{V1}(g)φ^S(x,u) and its inner theta series θ_{A,0} is the same with V0 in place of V1 (θ_{A,0} = 0 if V0 = ∅).
api: Nondegenerate V1=V, nontruncated V0 empty, nonsingular extension φ'_S(1)
outer/inner usual theta with their own V1/V0 Weil actions.
unitTests: The zero subspace and empty V0 are distinct truncations.
An arbitrary discontinuous or unbounded bad-place function does not define admissible pseudo-theta data.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits that φ^S ∈ S̄(V(A^S)×A^{S,×}) has STANDARD (Gaussian) archimedean components (the ρ∞ factor in (6.2.1) depends on it), that V is positive definite over F and V0 ⊂ V1 ⊂ V are F-subspaces with induced forms, all even-dimensional, and that the bounded-support condition is for each fixed g. Otherwise faithful.

items.name: Pseudo-theta comparison on a small bad-place compact
items.statement: Let A = A^{(S)}_{φ′} be a nonsingular pseudo-theta series on V0 ⊂ V1 ⊂ V (d = dim V, d_i = dim V_i; θ_{A,0} := 0 if V0 = ∅), with φ^S standard at the archimedean places. Let S′ ⊇ S be a finite set of nonarchimedean places outside of which φ_v is standard, compatible with the orthogonal splittings V = V1 ⊕ V1^⊥ = V0 ⊕ V0^⊥, and the discriminant characters χ_{V1^⊥}, χ_{V0^⊥} are unramified. Then there is an open compact K_{S′} ⊂ GL2(F_{S′}) such that for all g ∈ K_{S′}GL2(A^{S′}): A(g) = χ_{V1^⊥}(a(g)) ρ∞(g)^{(d−d1)/2} δ(g)^{(d−d1)/2} θ_{A,1}(g) − χ_{V0^⊥}(a(g)) ρ∞(g)^{(d−d0)/2} δ(g)^{(d−d0)/2} θ_{A,0}(g). Here δ(g) = ∏_{all v} δ_v(g_v) with δ_v([[a,b],[0,d]]k) = |a/d|_v^{1/2}; ρ∞(g) = ∏_{v|∞} e^{iθ_v} for g_v = [[a,b],[0,d]]k_{θ_v}, a > 0; and χ_W(a(g)) := ∏_{w∉S′ finite} χ_{W,w}(a_w), where a_w is the upper-left Iwasawa entry of g_w and χ_W is the quadratic character of the discriminant of W. The characters are trivial when the complement has square discriminant, e.g. for quaternionic complements. As printed (without the characters), the identity holds only where every χ_{W,w}(a_w) = 1.
proofOutline: Factor archimedean Gaussian/weight and compare finite local sections on a common right stabilizer.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Two real errors in the item, and one in the paper. (i) The item writes (ρ∞δ∞); (6.2.1) uses the full adelic δ(g) = ∏_{all v}δ_v(g_v). The finite part matters: the Lemma 6.1 proof uses δ(gg0) = δ∞(g)δ_f(g0). (ii) The identity holds for g ∈ K_{S′}GL2(A^{S′}), where S′ ⊇ S also contains the places at which φ_v is not standard, not for g_S in a small compact. (iii) The paper's (6.2.1) is itself missing an unramified quadratic character (new issue on p. 581): r_V(g)φ_w = δ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2} r_{V1}(g)φ_w fails by χ_{V1^⊥,w}(a_w). The corrected statement includes the character. Locator: (6.2.1) is on p. 581, not p. 582.

items.name: Automorphic sum reduces to nondegenerate outer theta
items.statement: Let {A_ℓ^{(S_ℓ)}}_ℓ be a finite set of nonsingular pseudo-theta series, A_ℓ sitting on V_{ℓ,0} ⊂ V_{ℓ,1} ⊂ V_ℓ. The positive definite even-dimensional F-quadratic spaces V_ℓ, the sets S_ℓ and the unit groups µ_ℓ may depend on ℓ. If Σ_ℓ A_ℓ(g) is automorphic on GL2(A), then Σ_ℓ A_ℓ = Σ_{ℓ∈L_{0,1}} θ_{A_ℓ,1}, where L_{0,1} = {ℓ : V_{ℓ,1} = V_ℓ}. Proof: Vandermonde in the values (1+iN)^{−[F:Q]} for distinct POSITIVE sufficiently divisible N (E12).
proofOutline: Separate codimension powers using weak approximation and a Vandermonde system; choose distinct positive integral lower-unipotent parameters, not arbitrary distinct integers.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item adds a restriction that Lemma 6.1 does not have: 'with common ambient V'. In the paper the ambient spaces V_ℓ, and also S_ℓ and µ_ℓ, may vary with ℓ. This matters: §9 applies the lemma to series on different nearby algebras B(v), so the item as written cannot be used there. Part (1) is unaffected by the missing-character issue on p. 581, because nondegenerate series have V_{ℓ,1}^⊥ = 0. Review note: Nothing in the atlas plans pseudo-theta series; missing and source-routed to GZ is right. The proofOutline's 'positive' repair matches E12 (confirmed).

items.name: Positive-codimension theta cancellation
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.1, suppose that for each k > 0 the orthogonal complements V_ℓ ⊖ V_{ℓ,1} (ℓ ∈ L_{k,1}) and V_ℓ ⊖ V_{ℓ,0} (ℓ ∈ L_{k,0}) all have the same quadratic discriminant character. Then Σ_{ℓ∈L_{k,1}} θ_{A_ℓ,1} − Σ_{ℓ∈L_{k,0}} θ_{A_ℓ,0} = 0, where L_{k,1} = {ℓ : dim V_ℓ − dim V_{ℓ,1} = k} and L_{k,0} = {ℓ : dim V_ℓ − dim V_{ℓ,0} = k}. Without the hypothesis the proof gives only the character-twisted identity on GL2(A_f^S).
proofOutline: Use the same distinct-value Vandermonde argument; isolate the codimension-two/weight-one identity needed in §9.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: As printed, Lemma 6.1(2) rests on (6.2.1), which lacks the discriminant characters (new issue, p. 581). The proof then gives Σ_{ℓ∈L_{k,1}} χ_{V_{ℓ,1}^⊥}(a(g0))θ_{A_ℓ,1}(g0) − Σ_{ℓ∈L_{k,0}} χ_{V_{ℓ,0}^⊥}(a(g0))θ_{A_ℓ,0}(g0) = 0 only for g0 ∈ GL2(A_f^S). The untwisted identity follows only when, in each codimension, all the complements have the same discriminant character. §9 meets this condition (codimension 2: complements E·j with character η; codimension 4: quaternionic complements with trivial character), so the application stands. The item should state the hypothesis. Also note that L_{k,*} is indexed by codimension k, which is always even.

items.name: Mixed theta–Eisenstein kernel
items.statement: Let B be a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra over A = A_F with E_A → B, and φ ∈ S̄(B×A^×) invariant under U×U. Then I(s,g,φ)_U = Σ_{u∈µ_U²\F^×} Σ_{γ∈P^1(F)\SL2(F)} δ(γg)^s Σ_{x1∈E} r(γg)φ(x1,u). For φ = φ1⊗φ2 with respect to B = E_A ⊕ E_A j, I(s,g,φ)_U = Σ_u θ(g,u,φ1)E(s,g,u,φ2), where θ(g,u,φ1) = Σ_{x1∈E} r(g)φ1(x1,u) and E(s,g,u,φ2) = Σ_γ δ(γg)^s r(γg)φ2(0,u). By incoherence I(0,g,φ) = 0.
items.locator: §7.1, pp. 583–584 (from [YZZ13, §5.1.1]); vanishing I(0,g,φ) = 0 stated in §1.3, p. 540
api: Meromorphic s-family, pure-tensor extension by linearity, Fourier expansion and derivative I'

items.name: Normalized local Whittaker terms
items.statement: For a place v, a ∈ F_v, u ∈ F_v^× and φ_{2,v} ∈ S̄(E_v𝔧_v×F_v^×), put W_{a,v}(s,g,u,φ_{2,v}) = ∫_{F_v} δ(wn(b)g)^s r(wn(b)g)φ_{2,v}(0,u) ψ_v(−ab) db. For a ∈ F_v^×, W°_{a,v} = γ_{u,v}^{−1}W_{a,v}, where γ_{u,v} is the Weil index of (E_v𝔧_v, uq). For a = 0, W°_{0,v}(s,g,u,φ_{2,v}) = γ_{u,v}^{−1}·(L(s+1,η_v)/L(s,η_v))·|D_v|^{−1/2}|d_v|^{−1/2}·W_{0,v}(s,g,u,φ_{2,v}), with D_v the relative discriminant of E_v/F_v and d_v the local different of F_v. Then W°_{0,v}(0,g,u) = r(g)φ_{2,v}(0,u) for all v, and W°_{0,v}(s,g,u) = δ_v(g)^{−s}r(g)φ_{2,v}(0,u) for almost all v and for every archimedean v. Globally W_0(s,g,u) = −(L(s,η)/L(0,η))/(L(s+1,η)/L(1,η))·∏_v W°_{0,v}(s,g,u), since ∏_vγ_{u,v} = −1 for incoherent B.
api: Fourier index a, s derivative, a=0 branch, character and measure changes
no a→0 continuity assumption for derivatives.
unitTests: Differentiate the normalization as well as the Whittaker integral.
YZZ13 Proposition6.10(1) cannot be used unchanged at a=0.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. For a ≠ 0, W°_{a,v} = γ_{u,v}^{−1}W_{a,v}, with the Weil index only: no L-ratio and no |D_v d_v| factor. Only W°_{0,v} carries γ^{−1}·L(s+1,η_v)/L(s,η_v)·|D_v|^{−1/2}|d_v|^{−1/2}. Also missing: the key properties W°_{0,v}(0,g,u) = r(g)φ_{2,v}(0,u) for all v, and W°_{0,v}(s,g,u) = δ_v(g)^{−s}r(g)φ_{2,v}(0,u) for almost all v and for archimedean v (Lemma 7.6(1)). items.name: Projected derivative decomposition
items.statement: Let F be totally real, E/F a totally imaginary quadratic extension with character η, B a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra over A_F with E_A → B, U ⊂ B_f^× open compact, and φ ∈ S̄(B×A^×) invariant under U×U, standard at every archimedean place, satisfying Assumption 7.1. Then Pr I′(0,g,φ)_U = −Σ_{v|∞} I′(0,g,φ)(v) − Σ_{v∤∞ nonsplit in E} I′(0,g,φ)(v) − c1·Ω_φ(g) − Σ_{v∤∞} Σ_{u∈µ_U²\F^×} Σ_{y∈E^×} c_{φ_v}(g,y,u) r(g)φ^v(y,u) + Σ_{u∈µ_U²\F^×} Σ_{y∈E^×} (2 log δ_f(g_f) + log|uq(y)|_f) r(g)φ(y,u). Here Ω_φ(g) = Σ_{u∈µ_U²\F^×}Σ_{y∈E^×} r(g)φ(y,u), and I′(0,g,φ)(v) = 2⨍_{C_U} K^{(v)}_φ(g,(t,t))dt is the normalized average over C_U = E^×\E^×(A_f)/(E^×(A_f)∩U). For v|∞, K^{(v)}_φ(g,(t1,t2)) = w_U Σ_{a∈F^×} lim_{s→0} Σ_{y∈µ_U\(B(v)^×_+ − E^×)} r(g,(t1,t2))φ(y)_a k_{v,s}(y), with k_{v,s}(y) = Γ(s+1)/(2(4π)^s)·∫_1^∞ dt/(t(1−λ(y)t)^{s+1}) and λ(y) = q(y2)/q(y) ∈ F_v. For finite nonsplit v, K^{(v)}_φ(g,(t1,t2)) = Σ_u Σ_{y∈B(v)−E} k_{r(t1,t2)φ_v}(g,y,u) r(g,(t1,t2))φ^v(y,u), with k_{φ_v}(g,y,u) = (L(1,η_v)/vol(E_v^1))·r(g)φ_{1,v}(y1,u)·W°′_{uq(y2),v}(0,g,u,φ_{2,v}) (y2 ≠ 0) for φ_v = φ_{1,v}⊗φ_{2,v}, extended linearly. c1 = 2L′_f(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F|, with L_f the finite part and d_E, d_F absolute discriminants. c_{φ_v}(g,y,u) = r_E(g)φ_{1,v}(y,u)W°′_{0,v}(0,g,u,φ_{2,v}) + log δ(g_v)r(g)φ_v(y,u) for pure tensors, extended linearly.
proofOutline: Differentiate the incoherent Fourier expansion, use YZZ holomorphic projection and the archimedean logarithmic integral, removing exactly the global gamma derivative. E10 fixes the intermediate c2 bookkeeping.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Missing hypothesis: φ standard at infinity (Theorem 7.2 assumes it together with Assumption 7.1). 'Σv' must run over the archimedean places AND the finite places nonsplit in E. Ω_φ is not defined in the item. The constant should read log|d_E/d_F|: d_E < 0 when [F:Q] is odd. The archimedean kernel is only named, not stated. The constants are correct. Recomputed: c0 = 2L′(0,η)/L(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F| from L(1−s,η) = |d_E/d_F|^{s−1/2}L(s,η); the per-place projection of log(y^{1/2})·y e^{−2πy} is 4π∫_0^∞ (1/2)log y·e^{−4πy}dy = −(1/2)(γ+log 4π), so c2 = −(m/2)(γ+log 4π); c1 = c0 − 2c2 (E10), and L′_∞/L_∞(0,η) = −(m/2)(γ+log 4π) gives c1 = 2L′_f(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F|. Review note: Its general shape is GZ.6's scope; the constant-term-retaining statement is specific to YZ18. Keep on the GZ source route.

items.name: Special test function and integral j
items.statement: Setting: F, E, B as in Theorem 1.7, with no finite place ramified in both E and B. U = ∏_{v∤∞}U_v is a maximal open compact subgroup of B_f^× containing Ô_E^×, and O_{B_v} is the O_{F_v}-algebra generated by U_v (a maximal order, U_v = O_{B_v}^×, O_{E_v} ⊂ O_{B_v}). Take φ = ⊗φ_v with: (1) v|∞: the standard Gaussian; (2) v finite, nonsplit in E, split in B: 1_{O_{B_v}×O_{F_v}^×}; (3) v nonsplit in B: 1_{O_{B_v}^××O_{F_v}^×}; (4) v ∈ S2, a set of two finite places split in E and unramified over ℚ: 1_{O_{B_v}^××O_{F_v}^×} − (1+N_v+N_v²)^{−1}·1_{ϖ_v^{−1}(O_{B_v})_2×O_{F_v}^×}, where (O_{B_v})_2 = {x ∈ O_{B_v} : v(q(x)) = 2}; (5) v split in E, v ∉ S2: 1_{O_{B_v}×O_{F_v}^×}. For each finite v, fix 𝔧_v ∈ O_{B_v} orthogonal to E_v with v(q(𝔧_v)) ∈ {0,1}, equal to 1 iff B_v is nonsplit (then E_v/F_v is inert). In the split-B case, 𝔧_v acts as Galois conjugation on O_{E_v} ≅ M = O_{F_v}², transported by t ↦ t·m0 with m0 an O_{E_v}-module generator of M, and q(𝔧_v) = −1.
api: primitive OE-module generator to identify OB=EndOF(OE)
unitTests: At a division place use units, not the full order.
At S2 the correction coefficient is 1/(1+q+q²), not 1/(q+1).
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the §7.2 setting: U = ∏U_v is a maximal open compact subgroup containing Ô_E^×, O_{B_v} is the order generated by U_v, and no finite place ramifies in both E and B. It also omits the defining conditions of S2 (two finite places split in E and unramified over ℚ). The item uses q both for the norm form and for N_v, which is ambiguous. The existence of 𝔧_v in the split-B case needs E11's fix (m0 an O_{E_v}-generator of M).

items.name: Integral order sandwich
items.statement: At a finite place, Dv OBv⊂OEv+OEv jv⊂OBv, with equality OEv+OEv jv=OBv iff E/F is unramified at v.
proofOutline: Compute trace-form discriminants 1 and Dv² and the explicit conjugation basis; compare indices.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): Minor: state the §7.2 setting (O_{B_v} ⊇ O_{E_v} the maximal order generated by U_v; 𝔧_v as chosen there; no common finite ramification of E and B) and that D_v is the relative discriminant. Verified: d_{O_{E_v}+O_{E_v}𝔧_v} = D_v²q(𝔧_v)², with q(𝔧_v) a unit when B_v is split, and a finite O_{F_v}-module of length v(D_v) is killed by D_v, which gives the sandwich.

items.name: Norm congruence shells and ramified correction
items.statement: For v finite and nonsplit in E, u ∈ O_{F_v}^× and a ∈ uq(E_v^×j_v) (the nearby line), put D_n(a) = {x2 ∈ E_v𝔧_v : uq(x2) − a ∈ p_v^n d_v^{−1}} and D_n = {x2 ∈ E_v𝔧_v : uq(x2) ∈ p_v^n d_v^{−1}}, with dx2 self-dual for (E_v𝔧_v, uq). Put α_v(y,u) = (log N_v/|D_v|^{1/2})·1_{D_v^{−1}O_{E_v}−O_{E_v}}(y)·Σ_{n=0}^{v(d_v)−1} N_v^n ∫_{D_n} φ_v(y+x2,u)dx2.
api: α has compact support away from OE.
unitTests: If v(dv)=0 the α sum is empty.
Do not confuse v(Dv), the relative different exponent, with v(dv).
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Clarify the two lines. D_n(a) and D_n are subsets of the ORIGINAL line E_v𝔧_v, with self-dual measure for (E_v𝔧_v, uq) and vol(O_{E_v}𝔧_v) = |D_v|^{1/2}|d_v u q(𝔧_v)|. The index a = uq(y2) is represented by the NEARBY line E_v j_v ⊂ B(v)_v. Also u ∈ O_{F_v}^×. The unit test calls v(D_v) 'the relative different exponent'; in the paper D_v is the relative DISCRIMINANT of E_v/F_v (Lemma 7.3), and d_v is the local different of F_v, i.e. the conductor exponent of ψ_v.

items.name: Inert norm-shell cutoff
items.statement: If Ev/Fv is unramified quadratic and a lies in the opposite nearby norm class, Dn(a)=Dn for n≤v(a dv), and Dn(a)=∅ for n>v(a dv).
proofOutline: Use opposite parity of the valuations of represented norms.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Verified: v(uq(x2) − a) = min(v(a), v(q(x2))) because the valuations have different parity.

items.name: Ramified norm-shell volume
items.statement: For ramified Ev/Fv, Dn(a)=Dn for n≤v(a dv), is empty for n>v(a dv)+v(Dv)−1, and for v(a dv)<n≤v(a dv)+v(Dv)−1 has volume |Dv|^1/2 |dv| |a| q^(v(a dv)−n).
proofOutline: Use the conductor of the local quadratic norm subgroup and index-two unit cosets, including wild/dyadic conductor.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Verified: e_v = v(D_v) (conductor = discriminant exponent), and the half-coset volume converts via dx = |a|ζ_{E_v}(1)^{−1}d^×x and vol(E_v^1) = 2|D_v|^{1/2}|d_v|^{1/2}.

items.name: Inert logarithmic singularity and diagonal extension
items.statement: For inert v with §7.2 data, kφv(1,y,u)−(1/2)φv(y1,u)1OEj(y2)(v(q(y2)/q(jv))+1)log q extends to a Schwartz function; its restriction to E is φv(y,u)(|dv qjv|−1)log q/((1+q^−1)(1−q)). The jv in the singular term is the original test-function j, not the nearby j.
proofOutline: Insert shell cutoff into normalized Whittaker derivative and evaluate finite geometric sums; verify source's nearby-line convention when implementing.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Image-checked: the indicator is 1_{O_{E_v}j_v}(y2) (nearby j), while q(𝔧_v) in v(q(y2)/q(𝔧_v)) and |d_vq(𝔧_v)| is the original; the item's note is right. The formula recomputes correctly; Prop. 9.2(1) cancels against Lemma 8.7(1).

items.name: Ramified logarithmic singularity and diagonal extension
items.statement: For ramified v with §7.2 data, subtract (1/2)φv(y1,u)1OEj(y2)(v(qy2)+1)log q from kφv(1,y,u). It extends to Schwartz; on E its value is φv(y,u)[(|dv|−1)/(2(1−q))+(v(Dv)−1)/2]log q+αv(y,u)/2.
proofOutline: Split the shell series into n<v(dv), n≤v(a dv), and the conductor tail; keep α on Dv^−1OE−OE.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Recomputed (7.3.2)–(7.3.4): (|d_v|−1)/(2(1−N_v)), (v(a)+1)/2 and (v(D_v)−1)/2 times log N_v; the lemma is correct. Misprints on p. 598: E22 ('does affect' → 'does not affect'), and vol(D_n) → vol(D_n(a)) in the first line of (7.3.4) (new).

items.name: Archimedean zero-term correction
items.statement: For standard archimedean φ and all g,y,u, cφv(g,y,u)=0.
proofOutline: Evaluate normalized W0(s) as δ(g)^−s r(g)φ(0,u); derivative cancels the logδ term.
