items.name: Finite zero-term correction
items.statement: For v non-archimedean, (y,u) ∈ E_v×F_v^× and φ as in §7.2. If v ∉ S2: c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = φ_v(y,u)·log|d_vq(𝔧_v)| plus φ_v(y,u)·2(|d_vq(𝔧_v)|−1)log N_v/((1+N_v^{−1})(1−N_v)) if E_v/F_v is inert; plus φ_v(y,u)·(|d_vq(𝔧_v)|−1)log N_v/(1−N_v) + α_v(y,u) if ramified; plus 0 if split. If v ∈ S2: c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2 log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))·1_{ϖ_v^{−1}(O_{B_v})_2}(y)·1_{O_{F_v}^×}(u), i.e. 2 log N_v·(φ_v(y,u) − 1_{O_{B_v}^××O_{F_v}^×}(y,u)); on E_v the set ϖ_v^{−1}(O_{B_v})_2 is {y ∈ ϖ_v^{−1}O_{E_v} : q(y) ∈ O_{F_v}^×}. Here α_v is as in Lemma 7.4.
proofOutline: Use the corrected a=0 Whittaker normalization; compute inert/ramified geometric series and the split norm-product volumes; verify both S2 summands separately.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: At v ∈ S2 the item copies a false case of Lemma 7.6(2). For v ∈ S2, |d_v| = |q(𝔧_v)| = 1 and the split-case entry '0' would give c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 0. In fact c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −2 log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²) on y ∈ ϖ_v^{−1}O_{E_v} with q(y) ∈ O_{F_v}^× and u ∈ O_{F_v}^× (new issue, pp. 603–604). The proofOutline's 'verify both S2 summands separately' is exactly where it fails: c_{ψ2} = 2 log N_v there. The other cases are verified: inert log|d q(𝔧)| + 2(|d q(𝔧)|−1)log N/((1+N^{−1})(1−N)), ramified log|d| + (|d|−1)log N/(1−N) + α_v, split v ∉ S2 log|d|. Theorem 9.1 is unaffected because Lemma 8.7(2) is off by the compensating amount at S2.

items.name: Picard-valued Hecke and height series
items.statement: Let F be totally real, 𝔹 a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra over A = A_F with ramification set Σ, |Σ| > 1, and U ⊂ 𝔹_f^× open compact; X_U is the projective smooth Shimura curve over F, X_{U,τ}(C) = B(τ)^×\h^± × 𝔹_f^×/U. For x ∈ 𝔹_f^× let U_x = U ∩ xUx^{-1} and let Z(x)_U be the image of (π_{U_x,U}, π_{U_x,U}∘T_x): X_{U_x} → X_U × X_U; it acts by [z,β]_U ↦ Σ_{y∈UxU/U}[z,βy]_U. For φ ∈ S(𝔹×A^×) invariant under U×U, set Z(g,φ)_U = Z_0(g,φ)_U + Z_*(g,φ)_U with Z_0(g,φ)_U = −Σ_{α∈F_+^×\A_f^×/q(U)} Σ_{u∈μ_U²\F^×} E_0(α^{-1}u, r(g)φ) L_{K,α} and Z_*(g,φ)_U = w_U Σ_{a∈F^×} Σ_{x∈U\𝔹_f^×/U} r(g)φ(x, a q(x)^{-1}) Z(x)_U, where μ_U = F^×∩U and w_U = |{±1}∩U|. Let E/F be a CM extension with a fixed embedding E_A ↪ 𝔹. For t ∈ E^×(A_f) let [t]_U = [z0,t]_U and t° = [t]_U − ξ_{U,t}, where ξ_{U,t} is the normalized degree-one Hodge class on the connected component of [t]_U. Define Z(g,(t1,t2),φ)_U = ⟨Z(g,φ)_U t1°, t2°⟩_NT with the Néron–Tate pairing on J_U(F̄)_C.
unitTests: A set-theoretic correspondence image loses push-forward multiplicities.
The constant Hodge part pairs trivially with degree-zero classes.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Standing hypotheses and two definitions are missing. B is a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra over A_F with ramification set Σ and |Σ| > 1 (so X_U is a projective curve with no cusps). φ ∈ S(𝔹×A^×) is invariant under U×U. Z(x)_U is the image of (π_{U_x,U}, π_{U_x,U}∘T_x): X_{U_x} → X_U×X_U, not an unspecified 'proper correspondence'. Z_0 is the Hodge-class term. The height series is defined for t1,t2 ∈ E^×(A_f), with a fixed embedding E_A ↪ 𝔹, and uses the Néron–Tate pairing on J_U(F̄)_C. Review note: The scope is planned by GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. That layer constructs CM divisors and correspondences on X_U by push-forward with multiplicities, ξ-normalized degree-zero classes and arithmetic extensions. 'missing' with a source route to GZ.6 is defensible, but 'planned' (GZ.6) would also be correct. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): status changed from missing to planned (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6). GZ.6 plans the CM divisors and correspondences on X_U, pushed forward with multiplicities, their ξ-normalized degree-zero classes and the arithmetic generating series. This paper's normalizations remain the source for that layer, and the item stays in its source route.

items.name: Automorphy and cuspidality of the height series
items.statement: For φ ∈ S(𝔹×A^×) invariant under U×U (|Σ| > 1), the series Z(g,φ)_U is absolutely convergent and is an automorphic form in g ∈ GL2(A) with coefficients in Pic(X_U×X_U)_C (Theorem 8.1 = [YZZ13, Th. 3.17]). Consequently, for t1,t2 ∈ E^×(A_f), the height series Z(g,(t1,t2),φ)_U = ⟨Z(g,φ)_U t1°, t2°⟩_NT is an automorphic form, and it is a cusp form by [YZZ13, Lemma 3.19].
items.locator: §8.1, Theorem 8.1, p. 606 (= [YZZ13, Theorem 3.17]); cuspidality of the height series: §8.1, p. 607 (= [YZZ13, Lemma 3.19])
proofOutline: Import the genuine Picard-valued modularity theorem, then apply the degree-zero height functional; original YZZ proof leaves remain open.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The coefficient group and hypotheses are omitted. Theorem 8.1 (= YZZ13 Th. 3.17) concerns Z(g,φ)_U with coefficients in Pic(X_U×X_U)_C, for φ U×U-invariant and |Σ| > 1. Cuspidality of the CM height series is not part of Theorem 8.1. It is stated on p. 607 and cites YZZ13 Lemma 3.19. Review note: Planned by GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6, which says 'Establish modularity of the curve-level Chow-valued series through the relevant product formula and theta construction'. The status should be 'planned' (GZ.6), not 'missing'. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): status changed from missing to planned (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6). GZ.6 plans 'modularity of the curve-level Chow-valued series through the relevant product formula and theta construction'. This paper's normalizations remain the source for that layer, and the item stays in its source route.

items.name: Diagonal coefficient and modified self-intersection
items.statement: Set Ωφ=Σu∈μU²\F* Σy∈E* r(g,(t1,t2))φ(y,u). The coefficient of t2 in Z*t1 is Ωφ/e, e=[E*∩U:μU]=[OE*:OF*] at maximal level. Define i0(t,t)=i(t,t)−Σv iv(t,t)logNv, where iv is the extended local diagonal pairing, not the actual global self-intersection.
items.locator: §8.1, pp. 608–609 (the coefficient of [t2]_U in Z_*(g)t1 and Ω_φ); Theorem 8.6(1)–(2), p. 616 (i_0 and i_v(t2,t2) = ∫_{C_U} ī_v(tt2,tt2)dt)
api: Proper-part subtraction, global versus extended local diagonal, orbit averaging and logNv=1 at infinity.
unitTests: E* excludes zero, while associated outer theta includes it.
Ordinary split extended diagonal is zero, not the global arithmetic self-height.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked. The coefficient of [t2]_U is w_U Σ_a Σ_{y∈E^×/(E^×∩U)} r(g)φ(t1^{-1}t2y)_a = Ω_φ(g,(t1,t2))/[E^×∩U:μ_U]. Under the §7.2 hypotheses (U maximal, Ô_E^× ⊂ U), [E^×∩U:μ_U] = [O_E^×:O_F^×].

items.name: Regularized archimedean multiplicity
items.statement: For distinct CM lifts use ms(γ)=Qs(1−2λγ), with Qs(t)=∫0∞(t+sqrt(t²−1)cosh u)^−1−s du. Define extended diagonal Green sums by excluding E* and taking the constant Laurent coefficient at s=0.
api: Domain t>1, Re(s)>0 convergence, meromorphic continuation with simple pole, constant-term operation and diagonal exclusion.
unitTests: Constant Laurent coefficient is not evaluation at a pole.
The omitted E* diagonal is restored only through Ωφ i0/e.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked. The sum runs over γ ∈ μ_U\(B_+^× − E^×), with B = B(v) the nearby algebra at the real place v and weight 1_U(β1^{-1}γβ2). The formal extension to β1 = β2 is on p. 610.

items.name: Archimedean proper-height expression
items.statement: At a real place, ivbar(Z*t1,t2)proper=Mφ^(v)(g,(t1,t2))−ivbar(t2,t2)Ωφ/e, where M is the regularized ms-weighted nearby-quaternion sum.
proofOutline: Subtract the explicit diagonal multiplicity and apply the off-diagonal Green expansion; justify meromorphic continuation separately.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent.

items.name: Finite local multiplicities and diagonal omission
items.statement: (i) Let v be finite and nonsplit in E, and B = B(v). The multiplicity function m is defined on 𝔥_{U_v} = B_v^× ×_{E_v^×} 𝔹_v^×/U_v away from the image of (1,1), with m(b^{-1},β^{-1}) = m(b,β). For distinct [β1]_U ∈ CM_U and [t2]_U ∈ C_U, ī_v(β1,t2) = Σ_{γ∈μ_U\B^×} m(γt_{2v}, β_{1v}^{-1}) 1_{U^v}((β_1^v)^{-1}γt_2^v) ([YZZ13, Lemma 8.2]). For all pairs, ī_v is defined by the same sum over γ ∈ μ_U\(B^× − E^×∩β1Ut2^{-1}), equivalently over (B^×−E^×) ∪ (E^× − β1U_vt2^{-1}). For (y,u) ∈ (B_v−E_v)×F_v^×, m_{φ_v}(y,u) = Σ_{x∈𝔹_v^×/U_v} m(y,x^{-1}) φ_v(x, uq(y)/q(x)). For (y,u) ∈ E_v^××F_v^×, n_{φ_v}(y,u) = Σ_{x∈(𝔹_v^×−yU_v)/U_v} m(y,x^{-1}) φ_v(x, uq(y)/q(x)). (ii) Let v be split in E, with ν1, ν2 above v and E_v diagonal in 𝔹_v ≅ M2(F_v). The function m_ν̄1 on GL2(F_v)/U_v is supported on N(F_v)U_v/U_v. For U_v = (1+p_v^rO_{𝔹_v})^×, m_ν̄1(n(b)) = 1/(N_v^{r−v(b)−1}(N_v−1)) when v(b) ≤ r−1. The function m_ν̄2 is the same with lower unipotents N^t, and m_v̄ = ½(m_ν̄1+m_ν̄2). The extended pairing is ī_ν(β1,t2) = Σ_{γ∈μ_U\(E^×−β1U_vt2^{-1})} m_ν̄(t2^{-1}γ^{-1}β1) 1_{U^v}(β1^{-1}γt2), and ī_v(t,t) = 0. Finally n_{φ_v}(y,u) = ½Σ_{x∈(N(F_v)U_v−U_v)/U_v} φ_v(yx,u) m_ν̄1(x) + ½Σ_{x∈(N^t(F_v)U_v−U_v)/U_v} φ_v(yx,u) m_ν̄2(x).
unitTests: nφ must omit the diagonal coset.
The split average includes ν1 and ν2, not ν2 twice (E16).
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The construction leaves out the extended local pairing ī_v itself (pp. 611 and 614). Propositions 8.3 and 8.5 and Lemmas 9.4 and 9.5 use that pairing. The item also gives the split-case multiplicity only in words. Use m_v̄ = ½(m_ν̄1 + m_ν̄2), as corrected by E16.

items.name: Nonsplit proper-height expression
items.statement: For nonsplit finite v, ivbar(Z*t1,t2)proper=Mφ^(v)+Nφ^(v)−ivbar(t2,t2)Ωφ/e, with M from mφ and N from nφ, and the distinct torus-translation conventions of Proposition8.3.
proofOutline: Separate B(v)*−E* terms from E* off-diagonal terms in the multiplicity sum and regroup through Hecke cosets.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent.

items.name: Ordinary multiplicity and local pairing
items.statement: Let v be split in E, with 𝔹_v ≅ M2(F_v), E_v the diagonal torus, and ν1 corresponding to the upper-left idempotent. For every open compact U and distinct CM points [β1]_U ∈ CM_U, [t2]_U ∈ C_U: ī_ν1(β1,t2) = Σ_{γ∈μ_U\E^×} m_ν̄1(t2^{-1}γ^{-1}β1) 1_{U^v}(β1^{-1}γt2). Here m_ν̄1: GL2(F_v)/U_v → Q is Zhang's ordinary multiplicity, supported on N(F_v)U_v/U_v. For U_v = (1+p_v^rO_{𝔹_v})^×, m_ν̄1(n(b)) = 1/(N_v^{r−v(b)−1}(N_v−1)) when v(b) ≤ r−1 ([Zha01, Lemma 5.5.1]). The same holds for ν2 with lower-triangular unipotents. Extended to all pairs by summing over γ ∈ μ_U\(E^×−β1U_vt2^{-1}), the formula gives ī_ν1(t2,t2) = 0 for every [t2]_U ∈ C_U.
items.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.4, pp. 613–614; ν2 version and m_v̄, i_v̄, pp. 614–615
proofOutline: At small level the only contributing global γ is unique modulo μ; pass to general level using projection and the factor [μU:μU'].
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Minor omissions. Lemma 8.4 holds for arbitrary open compact U; only the explicit formula for m_ν̄1 needs U_v = (1+p^rO_{𝔹_v})^×. The item leaves out the extension to equal points, where ī_ν1(t2,t2) = 0 (p. 614), and the ν2 version. The ν2 display on p. 614 is mislabelled m_ν̄1 (E16). Review note: The proof was checked. At small U^v the only contributing γ is γ0 mod μ_U, since diag(a,d) ∈ N(F_v)U_v forces diag(a,d) ∈ U_v. For general U use the projection formula with π^{-1}[β1]_U = [μ_U:μ_{U′}]^{-1}Σ_{u∈U/U′}[β1u]_{U′}.

items.name: Split proper height and zero extended diagonal
items.statement: For E-split v, ivbar(t,t)=0 and ivbar(Z*t1,t2)proper=Nφ^(v), the half-sum of the two ordinary unipotent multiplicities.
proofOutline: Use commutativity for the diagonal and change Hecke coset variables for the proper terms.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked, including the change of variables x_v ↦ t1^{-1}γt2x_v on p. 616. The formula uses the E16-corrected m_v̄ = ½(m_ν̄1+m_ν̄2). At v ∈ S2, N^{(v)}_φ is not zero (see the new issue on Lemma 8.7(2)).

items.name: Full local decomposition of the height series
items.statement: Let (B,E,U) be as in §7.2 with |Σ| > 1, and let φ ∈ S(𝔹×A^×) be U×U-invariant and satisfy Assumption 7.1. Then for all t1,t2 ∈ C_U and g ∈ GL2(A): Z(g,(t1,t2),φ)_U = −Σ_{v nonsplit in E}(log N_v)∫_{C_U} M^{(v)}_φ(g,(tt1,tt2))dt − Σ_{v∤∞} N^{(v)}_φ(g,(t1,t2)) log N_v − Σ_{v∤∞} j_v(Z_*(g,φ)t1,t2) log N_v − i_0(t2,t2)Ω_φ(g,(t1,t2))/[E^×∩U:μ_U]. Here log N_v = 1 for real v. i_0(t2,t2) = i(t2,t2) − Σ_v i_v(t2,t2) log N_v, with i_v(t2,t2) = ∫_{C_U} ī_v(tt2,tt2)dt the extended local pairing. M^{(v)} is given by Proposition 8.2 for v|∞ and Proposition 8.3 for finite v. N^{(v)} is given by Proposition 8.3 for nonsplit v and Proposition 8.5 for split v. N^{(v)}(g,(tt1,tt2)) = N^{(v)}(g,(t1,t2)) because only y ∈ E^× occurs.
proofOutline: Two auxiliary split places kill Hodge cross-terms; decompose proper horizontal and vertical intersections, isolate the self-term, and use CU-invariance of N.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The standing hypotheses of §8.1 are missing. (B,E,U) must be as in §7.2 (U maximal at every finite place and containing Ô_E^×, no finite place ramified in both E and 𝔹), with |Σ| > 1. φ must be U×U-invariant and satisfy Assumption 7.1. Heights are computed on X_{U,O_H}, where H is unramified above Σ(𝔹_f). The item also blurs the arguments: M^{(v)} is averaged over C_U at (g,(tt1,tt2)), while N^{(v)} and j_v are taken at (g,(t1,t2)). Review note: The derivation was checked: −i−j, then i = i_proper + (Ω/e)i(t2,t2), then the proper part comes from Propositions 8.2, 8.3 and 8.5. Note that N^{(v)} ≠ 0 at v ∈ S2 (see the new issue on Lemma 8.7(2)).

items.name: Supersingular inert local intersection
items.statement: For E-inert and B-split v, mφ(y,u)=φv(y1,u)1OEvjv(y2)·(v(qy2)+1)/2.
proofOutline: Use YZZ local deformation multiplicity with its inert norm classes; the nearby j belongs to the switched algebra.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked against Lemma 7.4(1): with the original 𝗃_v, v(q(𝗃_v)) = 0 at 𝔹-split v, so the singular parts of k and m·log N_v agree exactly. The j_v in 1_{O_{E_v}j_v} is the nearby j_v ∈ B(v)_v (italic in the paper), as the proofOutline says.

items.name: Wild-inclusive ramified local intersection
items.statement: For E-ramified and B-split v, mφ(y,u)=φv(y1,u)1OEvjv(y2)·(v(qy2)+v(Dv))/2, including wild ramification.
proofOutline: Use the corrected c=0 multiplicity (1/2)v(Dv λ), not the erroneous tame-only formula inherited from Zha01/YZZ; original Gross lifting proof remains a gate.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: This depends on the corrected [YZZ13, Lemma 8.6] (E15). I verified the c = 0 ramified value ½v(D_vλ(b)) from Gross's canonical lifting (see E15). The paper calls the step from the corrected table to the ramified case of Lemma 8.7(1) 'easy' and gives no computation. I did not rederive that sum. It is consistent with Prop. 9.2(1): the extra ½(v(D_v)−1) cancels the ½(v(D_v)−1) in Lemma 7.4(2). A new coverage item for the corrected multiplicity table is proposed below.

items.name: Superspecial local intersection
items.statement: For B-division (hence E-inert) v, mφ(y,u)=φv(y1,u)1OEvjv(y2)·v(qy2)/2.
proofOutline: Use the integral upper-half-plane multiplicity of Lemma8.8 and Bv*/Uv≃Z.

Review note: Checked from Lemma 8.8. The x-sum over 𝔹_v^×/U_v ≅ Z forces v(q(y)) = 0 and u ∈ O^×. On that support y1 ∈ O_{E_v}^×, y2 ∈ ϖO_{E_v}j_v and λ(y) = q(y2)/q(y), so ½v(λ(y)) = ½v(q(y2)).

items.name: Diagonal-correction local coefficient
items.statement: Let (U,φ) be as in §7.2. For every finite place v ∉ S2 and (y,u) ∈ E_v^××F_v^×, n_{φ_v}(y,u) = φ_v(y,u)·½v(q(y)). For 𝔹_v nonsplit this is identically 0, since v(q(y)) = 0 on supp φ_v; for v nonsplit in E and 𝔹_v split it is the c ≥ 1 sum Σ_c m(y^{-1},h_c)vol(E_v^×h_cGL2(O)∩M2(O)_n); for v split it is ½(v(a)+v(d)) for y = diag(a,d). For v ∈ S2: n_{φ_v}(y,u) = −(1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}·1_{ϖ_v^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2}(y)·1_{O_{F_v}^×}(u). The ψ1 part vanishes, and the ψ2 part equals ½((1+v(a))+(1+v(d))) = 1 on its support. With the corrected Lemma 7.6(2) at S2, c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))ψ2(y,u), so d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 0 still holds there.
proofOutline: Nonsplit split-algebra case omits conductor c=0; division case is zero; split case shell counts give v(a),v(d); S2 gives zero.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: False at v ∈ S2. Here φ_v = ψ1 − (1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2, with ψ1 = 1_{O_{𝔹_v}^×}⊗1_{O^×} and ψ2 = 1_{ϖ^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2}⊗1_{O^×}. Then n_{φ_v}(y,u) = −(1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2(y,u), for example n_{φ_v}(1,1) = −1/(1+N_v+N_v²). The printed formula gives φ_v(1,1)·0 = 0. The proofOutline's 'S2 gives zero' copies the paper's false claim on p. 619 (new issue). The formula is correct for v ∉ S2.

items.name: Superspecial multiplicity by uniformization
items.statement: For B-division and E-inert v, m(γ,β) vanishes unless qγ qβ is a unit and γ∈Ev*(1+OE,v πv jv); in that support m(γ,β)=v(λγ)/2.
proofOutline: Use Čerednik–Drinfeld formal uniformization, reduce to two sections of P¹ over OEv with nonrational reductions, and compute largest congruence exponent for γ=a+bj.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The proof was checked (reduction to P^1_{O_{E_v}}, γ = a + bj_v, m = v(b) = ½v(λ(γ))). It needs Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, which HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.5 plans (proposed coverage item below).

items.name: Vertical correction is nonsingular pseudo-theta
items.statement: Let v be finite, nonsplit in 𝔹 and inert in E, with (U,φ) as in §7.2 (U_v = O_{𝔹_v}^×, φ_v = 1_{O_{𝔹_v}^×}⊗1_{O_{F_v}^×}), and B = B(v), so B_v ≅ M2(F_v). Fix a lift Ṽ = Σ_i a_iW̃_i to Ω̂⊗O_{F_v^ur} of the vertical divisor V_1. For t1,t2 ∈ C_U: j̄_v(Z_*(g,φ)t1,t2) = Σ_{u∈μ_U²\F^×} Σ_{γ∈B^×} r(g,(t1,t2))φ^v(γ,u) l^{(t1,t2)}_{r(g)φ_v}(γ,u), where l^{(t1,t2)}_{φ_v}(γ,u) = Σ_{x∈𝔹_v^×/U_v} φ_v(x, uq(t1^{-1}γt2)/q(x)) 1_{O^×}(q(x)/q(t1^{-1}γt2)) (γ^{-1}z0·Ṽ) = (γ^{-1}z0·Ṽ)·1_{O^×}(q(γ)q(t2)/q(t1))·1_{O^×}(u), and γ^{-1}z0·Ṽ = Σ_i a_i1_{α_iF_v^×GL2(O_{F_v})}(γ^{-1}). This kernel is supported on finitely many cosets of GL2(O_{F_v}) in B_v^× and on u ∈ O^×. It therefore extends by zero to a Schwartz function on B_v×F_v^×, so j̄_v and j_v = ∫_{C_U} j̄_v(Z_*(g)tt1,tt2)dt are finite sums of nonsingular pseudo-theta series on the full space B(v). Remark 8.10: the same holds for any U_v-invariant φ_v with φ_v(0,u) = 0.
proofOutline: Represent the admissible vertical divisor by components of the uniformization tree; norm support yields compactness. E17 flags the printed component-fixing assertion; equivariant lift/descent must be proved, not assumed.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: By E17, the (t1,t2)-covariant form 'r(t1,t2)l_φ' rests on the false claim that t2 ∈ F_v^×GL2(O_{F_v}) fixes every component, so it is unjustified. The pseudo-theta conclusion still holds with a kernel that depends on (t1,t2) only through q(t1) and q(t2); this is the paper's own second display on p. 623. The item also leaves out Remark 8.10: it suffices that φ_v(0,u) = 0. Under the §7.2 data the unit-norm condition becomes q(γ) ∈ q(t1t2^{-1})O^×. Review note: Also planned in part by HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.5, which supplies the uniformization. No equivariant lift or descent is needed. The proofOutline's 'equivariant lift/descent must be proved' can be replaced by 'use the second display on p. 623 directly'.

items.name: Vertical correction vanishes at B-split places
items.statement: At a finite B-split place in the maximal-level setup, jv(Z*t1,t2)=0.
proofOutline: Use a smooth auxiliary-level cover with disjoint irreducible fiber components and descend their underlying component decomposition to the quotient.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked (p. 621). Take the auxiliary prime of §4.2 coprime to v. Then X_{U′} is smooth at v, its special fibre is a disjoint union of irreducible curves, and so is that of the quotient X_U. Hence V_t has no nonzero admissible vertical part at v.

items.name: Analytic–arithmetic difference is a finite pseudo-theta sum
items.statement: For §7.2 data, archimedean K−M=0; at finite nonsplit v, k−m logq extends to Schwartz; dφ=2nφ logq−cφ+(2logδ+log|uqy|)rφ extends to Schwartz on E. All but finitely many local differences vanish identically.
proofOutline: Use Lemmas7.4/7.6/8.7 and unramified Iwasawa covariance; combine with the vertical nonsingular series.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked against the itemized list on p. 626. At v ∈ S2, d_{φ_v} ≡ 0 holds only because the S2 errors in Lemmas 7.6(2) and 8.7(2) cancel (new issues).

items.name: Nonsplit diagonal cancellation
items.statement: Let v be finite and nonsplit in E, with (U,φ,𝗃_v,j_v) as in §7.2. For (y,u) ∈ E_v×F_v^×: 2k_{φ_v}(1,y,u) − 2m_{φ_v}(y,u)log N_v + d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_v·φ_v(y,u). Here k_{φ_v}(1,·) − m_{φ_v}·log N_v is the Schwartz extension from B(v)_v−E_v to B(v)_v×F_v^× of Lemmas 7.4 and 8.7, evaluated on E_v, and d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 2n_{φ_v}(y,u)log N_v − c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) + log|uq(y)|_vφ_v(y,u).
proofOutline: Insert inert or ramified singularity-subtracted restrictions. In the ramified case α cancels and the remaining v(Dv) term cancels the geometric multiplicity correction.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement is ambiguous about j. On the right-hand side it must be the §7.2 element 𝗃_v ∈ O_{𝔹_v} of the original algebra, with v(q(𝗃_v)) = 1 exactly when 𝔹_v is nonsplit, and not the nearby j_v ∈ B(v)_v. Only with 𝗃_v does Σ_{v∤∞} −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_v equal log(d_F d_𝔹). The variables should also be stated: (y,u) ∈ E_v×F_v^×, g = 1, and k − m·log N_v denotes the value on E_v of its Schwartz extension. Review note: Verified case by case. Inert 𝔹-split: 2(|d q𝗃|−1)log N/((1+N^{-1})(1−N)) cancels against c. Inert 𝔹-nonsplit: the same with |d q𝗃| = |d|/N. Ramified: α_v cancels and ½(v(D_v)−1) cancels between Lemma 7.4(2) and the corrected Lemma 8.7(1). In all cases 2n·log N_v + log|uq(y)|φ = 0.

items.name: Split diagonal cancellation
items.statement: For split finite v, dφ(1,y,u)=−log|dv q(jv)|φv(y,u).
proofOutline: 2n logq cancels log|q(y)|; u is a unit on support; use c-finite.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The statement is correct. Here 𝗃_v is the original §7.2 element, q(𝗃_v) = −1 at split v, so the right side is −log|d_v|_vφ_v. The proofOutline ('2n log q cancels log|q(y)|; use c-finite') fails at v ∈ S2. There n_{φ_v} = −(1+N+N²)^{-1}ψ2|_E ≠ φ·½v(q), and c_{φ_v}(1,·) = −(2log N/(1+N+N²))ψ2|_E ≠ 0 (the paper's Lemmas 8.7(2) and 7.6(2) both claim 0 there). The two cancel in d_{φ_v}, and log|uq(y)| = 0 on supp φ_v, so d = 0 = −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|φ_v. The outline should treat S2 separately.

items.name: Nonzero associated weight-one theta
items.statement: Let (F,E,𝔹,U,φ) be as in §7.2. The weight-one theta series θ_{Ω,1}(g) = Σ_{u∈μ_U²\F^×} Σ_{y∈E} r_E(g)φ(y,u), which is the outer theta series of Ω_φ, is not identically zero. Take g_v = [[0,1],[−1,0]] at v ∈ Σ_f ∪ S2 and g_v = 1 elsewhere. Every term r_E(g)φ(0,u) is ε times a nonnegative number, with ε = Π_{v∈Σ_f}λ(E_v/F_v,ψ_v) ∈ {±1}, and |r_E(g)φ(0,1)| > 0. At v ∈ S2, ∫_{E_v}φ_v(y,1)dy = (1−N_v^{-1})²(1 − 3/(1+N_v+N_v²)) > 0. So the finite sum over u ∈ O_F^{×,+}/μ_U² is nonzero.
proofOutline: Use the Weil action for E itself, not ambient B; compute rE(g)φ(0,1)>0 and rE(g)φ(0,u)≥0, then finite summation.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'Strictly positive' is not justified. At v ∈ Σ_f (E_v/F_v inert) the local factor is r_E(w)φ_v(0,u) = λ(E_v/F_v,ψ_v)·vol(O_{E_v}^×)·1_{O^×}(u). The Weil index λ = η_v(d_v) = (−1)^{v(d_v)} is −1 when F_v/Q_p has odd different exponent. Every u-term therefore has the same sign ε = Π_{v∈Σ_f}(−1)^{v(d_v)}. The constant term is nonzero, which is all the proof needs, but it need not be positive (new issue).

items.name: Modified self-intersection formula
items.statement: For the compact §7.2 datum, i0(P,P)/e=Lf'(0,η)/Lf(0,η)+(1/2)log(dE/F/dB), with e=[OE*:OF*].
proofOutline: Apply codimension-two cancellation to D=Pr I'−2Z; substitute local cancellation, Σfinite−log|dv qj|=log(dF dB), and nonzero weight-one theta.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The constants were rederived. c1 = 2L′_f(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + log(d_E/d_F) = 2L′_f/L_f + log(d_F d_{E/F}). Σ_{v∤∞} −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_v = log(d_F d_𝔹). The identity log(d_Fd_𝔹) + (2/e)i_0 − c1 = 0 gives i_0/e = L′_f/L_f(0,η) + ½log(d_{E/F}/d_𝔹), with e = [O_E^×:O_F^×]. This is Theorem 9.1. The sign of the codimension-two identity on p. 627 is consistent with D = PrI′ − 2Z. Prop. 9.2 holds at every place, but at S2 only after both S2 errors (Lemmas 7.6(2) and 8.7(2)) are corrected together; the theorem is unaffected.

items.name: Residue-normalized adjunction line

A fractional ideal quotient length is signed until containment is proved.

Review note: Checked: M = L_{O_H} ⊗ O(e^{-1}P) = ω ⊗ O(P) ⊗ ⊗_{Q≠P} O((1−e_Q^{-1})Q), since e_P = e, and Res(du/u ⊗ 1_P) = 1 does not depend on the choice of u.

items.name: Archimedean adjunction constant
items.statement: With Petersson norm ||dz||=2 Im z and Q0(t)=(1/2)log((t+1)/(t−1)), the limit of m0(z0,z1)−log(2 Im z1/|z1−z0|) as z1→z0 is 0, so −log||1||w=iw(P,P)/e.
proofOutline: Algebraically rewrite as (1/2)log(1+|z1−z0|²/(4Imz0 Imz1))−(1/2)log(Imz1/Imz0); both limits vanish.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The algebra was checked. With Q_0(t) = ½log((t+1)/(t−1)) and t = 1 + |Δ|²/(2y0y1), m_0 − log(2y1/|Δ|) = ½log(1+|Δ|²/(4y0y1)) − ½log(y1/y0), which tends to 0. The e·m_0 term comes from the e elements of μ_U\(E^×∩U).

items.name: Extended local diagonal vanishes at small away-v level
items.statement: For nonsplit finite v, with U'v sufficiently small and U'v normal in Uv away from v as in §9.2, ivbar([1]U',[1]U')=0. For split v it is zero without shrinking.
proofOutline: Bound support in a compact local subgroup; in a totally definite nearby algebra global units modulo central μ are finite; shrink the away-v level to exclude the noncentral cosets.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked. In the proof, B = B(v), so 'W_v = O_{B_v}^× if v is nonsplit in B' refers to the nearby algebra and is consistent. Shrinking U′^v inside Z·K_0, with Z the closure of μ_W and K_0 small normal, keeps μ_W and excludes the finitely many noncentral cosets.

items.name: Geometric realization of extended self-intersection
items.statement: Let (B,E,U) be as in §7.2 with |Σ| > 1, P = [1]_U ∈ X_U(H) (H the Hilbert class field of E), w a finite place of H over v, and R = O_{H_w^ur}. Let U′ = U_vU′^v, where U′^v ⊂ U^v is open, normal and small enough that X_{U′,R} is regular, E^× ∩ U′μ_U = μ_U, and Lemma 9.5 holds. Let π: X_{U′,R} → X_{U,R} be the projection. Then every irreducible component 𝒫′ of the divisor π^*𝒫_R is the image of a section Spec R → X_{U′,R} and occurs in π^*𝒫_R with multiplicity e = [O_E^×:O_F^×]. Moreover i_w(P,P) = ī_v(P,P) = ⟨π^*𝒫_R − e𝒫′, 𝒫′⟩, a proper intersection on the special fibre of X_{U′,R}. If v is split in E, both sides are 0.
proofOutline: Use small-level diagonal vanishing and the U/U' projection formula with central-unit correction. Establish the CM lift as a section separately; do not infer it from global étaleness of the coarse cover.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement is the paper's Lemma 9.4 plus the section property, and it is true. The printed reason 'π is étale' is false: π is ramified of index e at 𝒫′ (E18). The section property still holds, for the reason in E18's correction. U′_v = U_v contains O_{E_v}^×, so [1]_{U′} and all its U-translates [β]_{U′} are defined over the class field of E attached to E^×(E^×(A_f)∩U′). That field is unramified over H at w, so these points lie in X_{U′}(H_w^ur), and their closures in the proper R-scheme X_{U′,R} are sections by the valuative criterion. Multiplicity exactly e needs E^×∩U′μ_U = μ_U, which holds after shrinking U′^v. The intersection is then proper, and the identity follows from Lemma 9.5 and the projection computation on p. 635, which I checked: Σ_{β∈U^v/U′^v}1_{U′^v}(β^{-1}γ) = 1_{U^v}(γ), then divide by [μ_U:μ_{U′}]. The item's proofOutline only says 'establish the CM lift as a section separately'. To be complete it must carry the class-field argument above and state the regularity of X_{U′,R} and the condition E^×∩U′μ_U = μ_U, as in the corrected statement.

items.name: Finite adjunction lattice identity
items.statement: For the residue image N at a finite place w, Nw contains OHw and length(Nw/OHw)=iw(P,P)/e.
proofOutline: Pull to the small-level regular model; compare π*O(P/e)|P' with O(P')|P', take the ideal of π*P/e−P', and apply the proper intersection formula.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Checked (pp. 633–634). The cokernel of O(𝒫′ − e^{-1}π^*𝒫)|_{𝒫′} → O_{𝒫′} has length ⟨e^{-1}π^*𝒫 − 𝒫′, 𝒫′⟩, and this is ≥ 0 because e^{-1}π^*𝒫 − 𝒫′ is effective and meets 𝒫′ properly. Lemma 9.4 then gives e^{-1}i_w(P,P). The printed '⟨O(e^{-1}π^*𝒫 − 𝒫′, 𝒫′⟩' is a garbled bracket (new misprint). The result depends on the E18 repair.

items.name: Arithmetic adjunction for the CM point
items.statement: For compact §7.2 data, i0(P,P)/[OE*:OF*]=−h_LU(P).
proofOutline: Sum finite residue-lattice lengths and archimedean norms; the arithmetic degree of the residue-normalized line gives the identity.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: The assembly of Theorem 1.7 was checked. Theorem 9.1 (i_0/e = L′_f/L_f(0,η) + ½log(d_{E/F}/d_𝔹)) and Theorem 9.3 (i_0/e = −h_{L̄_U}(P)) give h_{L̄_U}(P_U) = −L′_f(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + ½log(d_𝔹/d_{E/F}). This is Theorem 1.7 exactly; e = [O_E^×:O_F^×] cancels, and the hypotheses are |Σ| ≥ 2, no common finite ramification, and U maximal with Ô_E^× ⊂ U. With Theorem 1.6 (2^{-g}Σh(Φ) = ½h_{L_U}(P_U) − ¼log(d_𝔹d_F)), d_𝔹 cancels and Theorem 1.1 follows: −½L′_f/L_f(0,η) − ¼log(d_{E/F}d_F). The reduction on p. 629 to deg(M̄|_P) = e^{-1}Σ_w i_w(1,1)log N_w was also checked.

items.name: Quaternionic CM Hodge height
items.statement: Assume that at least two places of F ramify in 𝔹 and that no finite place of F ramifies in both E and 𝔹. Let U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 of 𝔹_f containing Ô_E, and let P_U be the image of a CM point P ∈ X^{E^×}. Then h_{L̄_U}(P_U) = −L_f′(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + ½ log(d_𝔹/d_{E/F}), where d_𝔹 = N(disc 𝔹) and d_{E/F} is the norm of the relative discriminant.
items.locator: §1.3, Theorem 1.7, p. 539 (U fixed just before it); proof §9, Theorems 9.1 and 9.3, pp. 624–635
proofOutline: Combine modified self-intersection formula and arithmetic adjunction; retain the compactness hypothesis.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: U hypothesis: the proof (p. 591) needs O_{E_v} ⊂ O_{𝔹_v} at every v, which 'maximal U containing Ô_E^×' does not imply when a place v | 2 with residue field F_2 splits in E (new issue).

items.name: Averaged Colmez theorem in finite-Hecke normalization
items.statement: For every CM field E with maximal totally real F and [E:Q]=2g, with Yuan–Zhang's Faltings metric, 2^−gΣall 2^g CM types Φ h(Φ)=−(1/2)Lf'(0,η)/Lf(0,η)−(1/4)log(dE/F dF).
proofOutline: Choose a compact auxiliary incoherent quaternion datum satisfying disjoint finite ramification, combine corrected height bridge with quaternionic height, and cancel dB. The auxiliary-existence argument and all analytic/integral external inputs remain explicit gates.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Statement checked. It follows from Theorems 1.6 and 1.7: ½(−L′/L + ½ log(d_𝔹/d_{E/F})) − ¼ log(d_𝔹 d_F) = −½L′/L − ¼ log(d_{E/F} d_F). The auxiliary datum always exists, although the paper leaves this implicit (new coverage item). Take Σ(𝔹) = {archimedean places} ∪ S, with S a set of finite places of F inert in E (Chebotarev): S = ∅ if g ≥ 3 is odd, |S| = 1 if g is even, |S| = 2 if g = 1. Then |Σ(𝔹)| is odd and at least 2, A_E embeds because E_v is a field at every v ∈ Σ(𝔹), and a maximal order Ô_𝔹 ⊇ Ô_E exists.

items.name: Projective system of regular PEL models
items.statement: The models X'_{n,U'^p}, with n prime to d_B and U'^p contained in U'(N) for some N≥3 prime to p, form a projective system of regular schemes over O_℘. The special fibre of each above ℘ is a smooth curve if ℘∤n d_B and a relative Mumford curve if ℘ | d_B.
proofOutline: Fine moduli (Proposition 3.5) gives the transition maps; smoothness and the Mumford description come from Proposition 3.2 and the Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Statement matches Corollary 3.6, p. 556 exactly (case 1 of §3.2).

items.name: Comparison of the quaternionic and PEL p-divisible groups
items.statement: The p-divisible groups H|X_1^0 = (B_p/O_{B,p}) × X^0/O^1_{B,p} and H'|X_1'^0 are isomorphic, compatibly with the actions of Δ_0/O^1_{B,p} ⊂ Δ'_0/O^1_{B,p}.
proofOutline: As in Carayol [Car86, Prop. 4.4.3], transported along Proposition 4.2.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Statement correct. It already corrects the printed 'Δ̄_0/O^1_{B,p} ⊂ Δ̄_0/O^1_{B,p}' on p. 563 (new misprint). R18.2 cites Carayol 1986 but does not plan this comparison.

items.name: Finite-level comparison of connected components
items.statement: For every ideal n of O_F dividing a power of p and prime to d_B, and every sufficiently small open compact U^p ⊂ G(Q̂^p) depending on n, there is an open compact U'^p ⊂ G'(Q̂^p) such that X^0_{n,U^p} ≃ X'^0_{n,U'^p} over K = F̂_℘^ur.
proofOutline: As in Carayol [Car86, Prop. 4.5.5]: take quotients of the comparisons of Propositions 4.2 and 4.3 by matched level groups.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent.

items.name: Determinant lattice at the torus point
items.statement: Let L ⊃ K′ be finite and x″ ∈ X″_1(L) the image of (x,y) ∈ (X_1×Y_1)(L). Let N″ be the bundle on 𝒳″_{1,℘′} induced, through (X_1 ×_K Y_1)/Δ(F̂^×) ≅ X″_1, from N_{1,℘} ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−d_{B,℘}) (Theorem 4.10). Then N″_{x″} = det W(ℋ″_{x″}) ⊗ det W(ℋ″^t_{x″}) as O_L-lattices in N″_{x″} ⊗ L = ω^{⊗2}_{X″_{1,℘′},x″} ⊗ L. Proof: by Proposition 5.4 both sides equal det W(ℋ_x) ⊗ det W(ℋ^t_x) ⊗ O_L = N_{1,℘,x} ⊗ O_L.
items.locator: Corollary 5.5 and the display before it, pp575–576
proofOutline: Identify Hom_{O_{E,p}}(Ω(H''^t), Ω(H'')^∨) with Hom_{O_{B,℘}}(W(H^t), W(H)^∨)⊗O_K' via Proposition 5.4 and the O_E/O_B type computation, apply integral Kodaira–Spencer (Theorem 4.10), and take determinants.
items.note: No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18): statement corrected against the paper: Two problems. (a) The first clause is false. The completion of 𝒳″_{1,℘′} at x″ is not the universal deformation of ℋ″_{x″} as a bare p-divisible O_{E,p}-module: that deformation space has relative dimension 2 (the τ1- and τ2-lines move independently), while X″ is a curve. The paper's supporting identity (3), Hom_{O_{E,℘}}(W(H^t_x), W(H_x)^∨) = Hom_{O_{B,℘}}(…), compares modules of O_K-ranks 2 and 1 (new error). (b) The lattices live in the generic fibre of N″ ≅ ω^{⊗2}, not in ω^{-2}. Corollary 5.5 itself holds by a direct argument: by Proposition 5.4 the W(I^t_y)-twists cancel in det W(ℋ″) ⊗ det W(ℋ″^t), and with the E8 convention N_{1,℘,x} = det W(ℋ_x) ⊗ det W(ℋ^t_x). Review note: missing. It inherits the ramified-F_℘ gap of Proposition 5.4.

items.name: Two auxiliary split places
items.statement: A set S2 of two non-archimedean places of F, split in E and unramified over Q, such that for v ∈ S2 the group U_v is maximal and r(g)φ_v(0,u)=0 for all g ∈ GL2(F_v) and u ∈ F_v^×.
api: The set S2 and its two conditions as a predicate on (U, φ)
the §7.2 test function at S2 satisfies it
unitTests: The function Lφ0 − deg(L)φ0 with L = 1_{(O_Bv)_2} satisfies r(g)φ_v(0,u)=0.
The standard function 1_{O_Bv}⊗1_{O_Fv^×} alone does not.
items.note: This is exactly [YZZ13, Assumption 5.4]. No exact declaration located in the bounded pinned-library/atlas screen. Source route supplies a finer specialized target, not a claim that its broad owner is absent. Review note: Matches Assumption 7.1 (p. 587) and [YZZ13, Assumption 5.4]. Checked that the §7.2 S2 function satisfies it: ∫_{B_v}φ_v = vol(O_B^×) − vol(ϖ^{−1}(O_B)_2)/(1+N+N²) = 0, since vol((O_B)_2) = (1+N+N²)N^{−4}vol(O_B^×); and ψ_v is unramified at S2, so r(g)φ_v(0,u) = 0 for all g.

items.name: Faltings height of a CM type
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field with CM by O_E of type Φ: O_E ⊂ End(A), [E:Q] = 2 dim A, and O_E acts on Lie(A)⊗C through Φ. (i) (Serre–Tate) There is a number field K ⊂ C over which A is defined and has a smooth projective model over O_K. (ii) (Colmez [Col93]) The Faltings height h(A) of §1.1 depends only on Φ; put h(Φ) := h(A). (iii) h(Φc) = h(Φ), because A with the conjugated O_E-action has type Φc. With the action γ ↦ γ^t of p. 544, A^t has type Φc, so h(A^t) = h(A). Given h(A^t) = h(A) (Raynaud) for all A, (ii) also follows from Theorems 2.2 and 2.3.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 535 ('Colmez proved that the height h(A_Φ) depends only on the CM type Φ'); used in Theorems 1.1, 1.6 and 2.3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): h(Φ) is the object of Theorems 1.1, 1.6 and 2.3 and no item defines it. cm-height-invariance is the component version and faltings-height is general. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: CM point on X_U and its Hodge height
items.statement: Let (𝔹, E, U) be as in quaternion-datum and let X = lim X_U carry its right 𝔹_f^×-action. X^{E^×} is the set of points of X fixed by E^× through the fixed embedding A_E → 𝔹 (terminology of [YZZ13, §§1.2–1.3, 3.1]). For P ∈ X^{E^×}, P_U ∈ X_U(E^ab) is its image and P̄_U is the Zariski closure of P_U in the integral model 𝒳_U of §4.2. Define h_{L̄_U}(P_U) := deĝ(L̄_U|_{P̄_U})/[F(P_U):F], where L̄_U is the arithmetic Hodge bundle of Theorem 4.7 with ||dz|| = 2 Im z. This does not depend on the choice of P: X^{E^×} is one Gal(E^ab/E)-orbit and the height is Galois invariant.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): The left side of Theorem 1.7 and the right side of Theorem 1.6. No item defines X^{E^×}, P_U or this height; hodge-qline supplies only L̄_U. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Existence of an auxiliary quaternion datum
items.statement: For every CM extension E/F with [F:Q] = g there are the following: a totally definite incoherent quaternion algebra 𝔹 over A_F with an A_F-embedding A_E → 𝔹, at least two places of F ramified in 𝔹, and no finite place ramified in both E and 𝔹; and a maximal order Ô_𝔹 of 𝔹_f containing Ô_E. Proof: by Chebotarev choose a finite set S of finite places of F inert in E with g + |S| odd and at least 2 (S = ∅ if g ≥ 3 is odd, |S| = 1 if g is even, |S| = 2 if g = 1), and let 𝔹 ramify exactly at the archimedean places and at S. E_v is a field at every ramified v, so A_E embeds, and every order of 𝔹_f lies in a maximal order.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 536 (implicit in the deduction of Theorem 1.1)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Needed to deduce Theorem 1.1. The averaged-colmez outline flags it as a gate, but no item states it, and the argument is short. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Integral de Rham cohomology of a CM abelian scheme
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p and 𝒜/O an abelian scheme with O_E ⊂ End(𝒜) and [E:Q] = 2 dim 𝒜, of CM type Φ. Then H^1_dR(𝒜/O) is free of rank one over O ⊗_Z O_E. In the Hodge filtration 0 → Ω(𝒜) → H^1_dR(𝒜/O) → H^1(𝒜, O_𝒜) → 0, the outer terms are free O-modules on which O_E acts with types Φ and Φc.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): This is the key external input of Lemma 2.4, cited but not proved in the paper, and it has no item. hodge-polynomial-sequence only mentions it in its outline. Route: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory.

items.name: Same-type CM p-divisible groups are isomorphic
items.statement: Let A and B over a number field K have CM by O_E of the same type Φ and good-reduction models 𝒜 and ℬ over O_K, and let σ | p be a finite place of K. Then Hom_{O_E⊗Z_p}(𝒜[p^∞], ℬ[p^∞]) over O_σ is free of rank one over O_E⊗Z_p and is generated by an isomorphism, and End_{O_E⊗Z_p}(𝒜[p^∞]_{O_σ}) = O_E⊗Z_p. Proof: after enlarging K, A and B are O_E-isogenous; T_pA and T_pB are free of rank one over O_E⊗Z_p, and G_K acts on both through the same character to (O_E⊗Z_p)^×; Tate's theorem gives Hom_{O_σ} = Hom_{K_σ}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Key step of Theorem 2.2 with no item. It needs Tate's full faithfulness for p-divisible groups and the equality of the CM Galois characters. Route: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory.

items.name: CM points of X′ and their abelian varieties
items.statement: (Case 2: E ⊂ B over F.) Let T′ ⊂ G′ be the subgroup of (b, e) with b, e ∈ E^×. The T′-fixed subscheme X′^{T′} of X′ is one T̂′-orbit, a principal homogeneous space under T̂′ modulo the closure of T′(Q); in the complex uniformization it is {[z0, t] : t ∈ T̂′}, where z0 is the unique T-fixed point of h. Each P′ ∈ X′^{T′} represents an abelian variety A_{P′} that is O_E-isogenous to A_{Φ1} × A_{Φ2}. For P′ = [z0, 1] and Λ = O_B ⊇ O_E, A_{P′} = (B⊗R)/O_B, with complex structure making left E-multiplication of type Φ1 on E⊗R and Φ2 on Ej⊗R.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): The source of A0 in Theorem 1.6 (p. 577) and Erratum §1. cm-alignment chooses the point but does not describe X′^{T′} or A_{P′}. Route: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.

items.name: Case-2 p-divisible group on X′
items.statement: (Case 2, U′ small enough for a universal A_{U′}.) The p-divisible group H′_{U′} := A_{U′}[p^∞] is isomorphic to (B_p/O_B,p × X′)/U′. Here U′ acts on B_p/O_B,p through its projection to O_B,p^× ×_{O_F,p^×} O_E,p^×, by x·(b, e) = e x b. It is the restriction to X′ of the group H″ of §5.1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Used as H′ = H″|X′ in §5.1 (p. 573). pel-pdiv covers only the case-1 group of §3.2. Route: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.

items.name: Projective system of quaternionic models over O_F and small-level reduction type
items.statement: The schemes 𝒳_U, for open compact U = ∏U_v ⊂ B_f^× maximal at every prime ramified in B (defined as 𝒳_{U′}/(Ū/Ū′) with U′ = U^pU_p(p), p ∤ 2d_B, U_p maximal), form a projective system of normal projective flat curves over O_F extending {X_U}. If U ⊂ U(N) = (1+NÔ_B)^× for some N ≥ 3, then 𝒳_U is smooth over O_F at every prime ℘ ∤ d_B with U_℘ maximal and is a relative Mumford curve at every prime ℘ | d_B.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): The global projective system of models over O_F, and its small-level reduction type at the primes where U_℘ is maximal, is used for the pullback compatibility in Theorem 4.7 and in Part II. qfactorial covers only part (2), and quaternion-regular-model is local at one ℘ with principal level at p. Route: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.

items.name: Integral models of X″ and X′ at ℘′ induced from 𝒳_{1,℘}
items.statement: Let ℘′ | p be a place of F′ over the place ℘ of F, K = F̂^ur_℘ and K′ = F̂′^ur_℘′. All geometric points of Y_1 are defined over K′, so Y_{1,℘′} is a principal homogeneous space of Ē^×∖Ê^×/O^×_{E,p}. The isomorphism f_℘′: (X_{1,℘} ×_K Y_{1,℘′})/Δ(F̂^×) ≅ X″_{1,℘′} = X″_1 ⊗_{F′} K′, together with the integral model 𝒳_{1,℘} and Spec O_{K′}, induces an integral model 𝒳″_{1,℘′} of X″_{1,℘′}; the embedding X′ → X″ then induces a model 𝒳′_{1,℘′}. If ℘ ∤ d_B both are smooth over O_{K′}. If ℘ | d_B both are stable Mumford curves, which are not regular when ℘ is ramified in F′. The line bundle N_{1,℘} ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−d_{B,℘}) on 𝒳_{1,℘} induces line bundles N′_{1,℘′} and N″_{1,℘′}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Corollary 5.5 and Proposition 5.7 compare lattices on these models, but no item constructs them or records their reduction type (smooth, or a stable Mumford curve that is not regular when ℘ ramifies in F′). Route: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.

items.name: Uniqueness of a CM p-divisible group of given type
items.statement: Let E_w/Q_p be finite, K_σ a p-adic field containing the Galois closure of E_w, Ŏ_σ the completion of the maximal unramified extension of O_σ, and Θ ⊂ Hom_{Q_p}(E_w, K_σ). Any two p-divisible groups over Ŏ_σ with an O_w-action making the Tate module free of rank 1 over O_w and with Lie algebra of type Θ are O_w-isomorphic. Over O_σ this uniqueness holds only up to unramified twist. (Cited as [CCO, p. 173, Proposition 3.7.4(1)].)
items.locator: Erratum, §2, p. 4 and Proposition 4, p. 7, citing [CCO, Proposition 3.7.4(1)]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Both the transfer of Theorem 2 to G_Θ and the identification G(𝔐_Θ) ⊗ Ŏ_σ ≅ Ğ_Θ in Proposition 4 rest on this external theorem, which is otherwise only an API line in formal-cm-type. Route: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory.

items.name: Kisin classification of connected finite flat group schemes, compatible with isogenies
items.statement: With O_σ, 𝔖 and Eis(u) as in kisin-classification, let (Mod/𝔖)^c be the category of 𝔖-modules 𝔐 of projective dimension 1 killed by a power of p, with a φ-semilinear φ: 𝔐 → 𝔐 whose linearization has image containing Eis(u)𝔐 and whose composites ψ_n factor through (p,u)φ^{n*}𝔐 for n ≫ 0. There is an exact equivalence 𝔐 ↦ G(𝔐) from (Mod/𝔖)^c to connected finite flat group schemes over O_σ [Ki09, Th. 1.3.9]. For an exact sequence 0 → 𝔐_{−1} → 𝔐_0 → 𝔐 → 0 with 𝔐_{−1}, 𝔐_0 ∈ BT^{φ,f}_{/𝔖} and 𝔐 ∈ (Mod/𝔖)^c, the induced map G(𝔐_{−1}) → G(𝔐_0) is an isogeny with kernel G(𝔐). In particular G(𝔐_Θ/δ_w𝔐_Θ) ≅ G_Θ[δ_w], O_w-linearly.
items.locator: Erratum, §2 ('Kisin's module for G_Θ[δ_w]'), p. 8, citing [Ki09, Theorem 1.3.9, p. 603]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 5 yields an isomorphism of torsion Kisin modules, and converting it into an O_w-isomorphism G_Θ[δ_w] ≅ G_Θ′[δ_w] needs this classification theorem. kisin-torsion is only a construction.

items.name: The integral kernel of the nearby isogeny is a graph
items.statement: In the setting of erratum Theorem 1, enlarge K so that A_i[δ_{E/F}] and A_i^t[δ_{E/F}] are constant. Let f̃: 𝒜1 × 𝒜2 → 𝒜 be the extension of f to the Néron models and 𝒬 = ker f̃. For every finite place σ of K, the two projections induce isomorphisms 𝒜1[δ_{E/F}]_{Ŏσ} ← 𝒬_{Ŏσ} → 𝒜2[δ_{E/F}]_{Ŏσ}. Equivalently, 𝒬_{Ŏσ} is the graph of an O_E-isomorphism 𝒜1[δ_{E/F}]_{Ŏσ} ≅ 𝒜2[δ_{E/F}]_{Ŏσ} extending the generic one. Consequently 𝒬_{Ŏσ} ≅ 𝒬^t_{Ŏσ} O_E-linearly (via Theorem 2 applied to A1^t and A1), and O_E acts on 𝒬 through O_E/δ_{E/F}, on which conjugation is trivial.
items.locator: Erratum, §3, proof of Theorem 1, display (5) and its proof, pp. 10–11
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): This is the step that links Theorem 2 to Proposition 6: the integral kernel is again a graph. corrected-nearby mentions it only in its proof outline. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Kernel of the dual isogeny is the Cartier dual of the kernel
items.statement: Let f: 𝒳 → 𝒴 be an isogeny of abelian schemes over a base S with kernel 𝒬, a finite locally free commutative group scheme. The kernel of the dual isogeny f^t: 𝒴^t → 𝒳^t is canonically isomorphic to the Cartier dual 𝒬^D. If f is O_E-linear, the isomorphism is O_E-linear for the dual actions γ ↦ γ^t on 𝒴^t and on 𝒬^D.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 6 computes ord_σ(det f^{t*}) as ℓ_σΩ(Q^t, τ^c), which uses ker(f^t) = (ker f)^D with the O_E-actions matched. The cartier-duality library item does not provide this. Route: ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.

items.name: Iwasawa invariants δ and ρ∞ on GL2(A)
items.statement: For a place v and g ∈ GL2(F_v), write g = [[a,b],[0,d]]k with k ∈ GL2(O_{F_v}) (v finite) or k = [[cos θ, sin θ],[−sin θ, cos θ]] and a > 0 (v real). Put δ_v(g) = |a/d|_v^{1/2}, which is independent of the decomposition and extends the character of P(F_v), and for real v put ρ_v(g) = e^{iθ}. For g ∈ GL2(A), δ(g) = ∏_v δ_v(g_v), δ_f and δ_∞ are its finite and archimedean parts, and ρ∞(g) = ∏_{v|∞}ρ_v(g_v). For g_N = [[1,0],[N,1]] ∈ GL2(F_∞), ρ∞(g_N)δ∞(g_N) = (1+iN)^{−[F:Q]}.
items.locator: §6.2, 'Approximation by induced theta series', p. 580; value at g_N in the proof of Lemma 6.1, p. 583
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Used by (6.2.1), Lemma 6.1 and the log δ_f terms of Theorem 7.2; no item defines them. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Restriction of the Weil representation to a subspace
items.statement: Let V1 ⊂ V be nondegenerate even-dimensional quadratic spaces over F_w (d = dim V, d1 = dim V1), and let φ_w be standard for the splitting V = V1 ⊕ V1^⊥: at finite w the characteristic function of a self-dual lattice that splits orthogonally, times 1_{O^×}, with ψ_w unramified; at real w the Gaussian. Then for g = [[a,b],[0,d]]k (Iwasawa, a > 0 at real w) and (x,u) ∈ V1(F_w)×F_w^×: r_V(g)φ_w(x,u) = χ_{V1^⊥,w}(a)·δ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2}·r_{V1}(g)φ_w(x,u) if w is finite, and r_V(g)φ_w(x,u) = ρ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2}δ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2}r_{V1}(g)φ_w(x,u) if w is real. Here χ_{V1^⊥} is the (unramified) quadratic character of disc(V1^⊥); the paper omits the character at finite w.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): This local identity drives (6.2.1). As printed it lacks the discriminant character (new issue), so it needs its own item with the corrected statement. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.

items.name: Derivative of the mixed theta–Eisenstein series before projection
items.statement: For φ ∈ S̄(B×A^×) invariant under U×U (B incoherent): W_0(s,g,u) = −(L(s,η)/L(0,η))/(L(s+1,η)/L(1,η))·∏_v W°_{0,v}(s,g,u), with L(s,η) completed. This gives the analytic continuation of the constant term. Moreover I′(0,g,φ) = −Σ_{v nonsplit} I′(0,g,φ)(v) − c0 Σ_{u∈µ_U²\F^×}Σ_{y∈E} r(g)φ(y,u) − Σ_v Σ_u Σ_{y∈E} c_{φ_v}(g,y,u) r(g)φ^v(y,u) + 2 log δ(g) Σ_u Σ_{y∈E} r(g)φ(y,u), where c0 = d/ds|_{s=0} log(L(s,η)/L(s+1,η)) = 2L′(0,η)/L(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F|, by L(1−s,η) = |d_E/d_F|^{s−1/2}L(s,η). Only finitely many v contribute.
items.locator: §7.1, 'Decomposition of the constant term', pp. 585–586 (from [YZZ13, §6.1.2, Prop. 6.7])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): The key intermediate identity: the constant term E′_0 kept here is what produces c1 and the log δ terms. Only projected-derivative's proof outline mentions it. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Archimedean holomorphic projection of log δ∞·W^(2)
items.statement: Let W^(2)(g_∞) = ∏_{v|∞} W_v^(2), with W_v^(2)(diag(y,1)) = y e^{−2πy}1_{y>0}. Under the holomorphic-projection formula of [YZZ13, Prop. 6.12], whose per-place factor is 4π lim_{s→0}∫_0^∞ y^s W(y) W^(2)(y) dy/y² (so that W^(2) projects to itself), log δ_v(g_v)·W^(2)(g_∞) projects to −(1/2)(γ+log 4π)·W^(2)(g_∞). Hence log δ∞(g)W^(2)(g_∞) projects to c2·W^(2)(g_∞) with c2 = −([F:Q]/2)(γ+log 4π). Consequently c1 = c0 − 2c2 = 2L′(0,η)/L(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F| + [F:Q](γ+log 4π) = 2L′_f(0,η)/L_f(0,η) + log|d_E/d_F|, using L_∞(s,η) = Γ_ℝ(s+1)^{[F:Q]} and L′_∞/L_∞(0,η) = −([F:Q]/2)(γ+log 4π).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): This is where E10 sits. It deserves a separate checkable statement with the recomputed constants. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Local Whittaker series for incoherent sections
items.statement: Let v be finite, u ∈ O_{F_v}^× and φ_{2,v} ∈ S̄(E_v𝔧_v×F_v^×). For a ∈ F_v^×: W°_{a,v}(s,1,u,φ_{2,v}) = |d_v|^{1/2}(1−N_v^{−s}) Σ_{n≥0} N_v^{−ns+n} ∫_{D_n(a)} φ_{2,v}(x2,u)dx2. For a = 0: W_{0,v}(s,1,u,φ_{2,v}) = γ_{u,v}|d_v|^{1/2}(1−N_v^{−s}) Σ_{n≥0} N_v^{−ns+n} ∫_{D_n} φ_{2,v}(x2,u)d_ux2. Here dx2 is the self-dual measure for (E_v𝔧_v, uq), with vol(O_{E_v}𝔧_v) = |D_v|^{1/2}|d_v u q(𝔧_v)|; YZZ13 Prop. 6.10(1) as stated is correct only for a ≠ 0. Hence, for every φ_v and extending linearly: k_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = (L(1,η_v)/vol(E_v^1))·d/ds|_{s=0}[|d_v|^{1/2}(1−N_v^{−s})Σ_n N_v^{−ns+n}∫_{D_n(a)} φ_v(y1+x2,u)dx2] with a = uq(y2); and c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = d/ds|_{s=0}[|D_v|^{−1/2}(L(s+1,η_v)/L(s,η_v))(1−N_v^{−s})Σ_n N_v^{−ns+n}∫_{D_n} φ_v(y+x2,u)d_ux2].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): These are the inputs to Lemmas 7.4 and 7.6. The a = 0 formula is the corrected one (E13). No item states them. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Archimedean derivative kernel
items.statement: For a real place v, let B(v) be the nearby quaternion algebra (split at v), with y = y1 + y2 ∈ B(v)_v = E_v + E_v j and λ(y) = q(y2)/q(y) ∈ F_v (λ(y) < 0 on B(v)^×_+ − E^×). Put k_{v,s}(y) = Γ(s+1)/(2(4π)^s)·∫_1^∞ dt/(t(1−λ(y)t)^{s+1}) and K^{(v)}_φ(g,(t1,t2)) = w_U Σ_{a∈F^×} lim_{s→0} Σ_{y∈µ_U\(B(v)^×_+ − E^×)} r(g,(t1,t2))φ(y)_a k_{v,s}(y), where φ(y)_a is YZZ13's a-th Whittaker coefficient notation. Then I′(0,g,φ)(v) = 2⨍_{C_U}K^{(v)}_φ(g,(t,t))dt is the holomorphic projection of the v-part [YZZ13, Prop. 6.15].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Part of Theorem 7.2's statement. projected-derivative only names it, and §9 (K − M = 0 at v|∞, via [YZZ13, Prop. 8.1]) compares it with arch-proper's M. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Corrected CM multiplicity at 𝔹-split, E-nonsplit places
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of F nonsplit in E and split in 𝔹, and B = B(v), so B_v is the division algebra. Let U_v = GL2(O_{F_v}). For c ≥ 0 write E_v^×h_cGL2(O_{F_v}) for the elements β whose lattice has multiplier ring O_{F_v} + ϖ_v^cO_{E_v}. The multiplicity function m on B_v^× ×_{E_v^×} GL2(F_v)/GL2(O_{F_v}), defined away from the image of (1,1), satisfies m(b,β) ≠ 0 only if q(b)q(β) ∈ O_{F_v}^×. In that case, for β ∈ E_v^×h_cGL2(O_{F_v}) and λ(b) = q(b2)/q(b) (b = b1 + b2, b1 ∈ E_v, b2 ⊥ E_v): m(b,β) = ½(v(λ(b))+1) if c = 0 and E_v/F_v is unramified; m(b,β) = ½v(D_vλ(b)) if c = 0 and E_v/F_v is ramified (tame or wild); m(b,β) = N_v^{1−c}(N_v+1)^{-1} if c > 0 and E_v/F_v is unramified; m(b,β) = ½N_v^{−c} if c > 0 and E_v/F_v is ramified. Proof of the c = 0 ramified case: by Gross's theorem, End of the canonical lifting mod π_E^m is O_E + π_E^{m−1}O_{B_v}, so 2m(b,β) = 1 + max_{a∈O_E}v(N(b1−a) + q(b2)). The quotient −q(b2)/N(t) is a non-norm, and 1+p^{v(D_v)} ⊂ N(E_v^×) while 1+p^{v(D_v)−1} is not, so the maximum is v(λ(b)) + v(D_v) − 1.
items.locator: §8.3, proof of Lemma 8.7, p. 618 (correcting [YZZ13, Lemma 8.6] and [Zha01, Lemma 5.5.2])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): This is the four-case table of local CM multiplicities at E-nonsplit, 𝔹-split places. It is the key input to Lemma 8.7(1)(2) and the place where E15 lives. No item states it; local-m-ramified states only a consequence. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Hodge-class terms vanish and the height series splits into horizontal and vertical parts
items.statement: Let (B,E,U) be as in §7.2 with |Σ| > 1, and let φ be U×U-invariant and satisfy Assumption 7.1. Let H/F be finite, with every point of CM_U defined over H and H unramified above Σ(𝔹_f), so that X_{U,O_H} is Q-factorial (Cor. 4.6). Use ξ̂-admissible arithmetic extensions on X_{U,O_H} ([YZZ13, §7.1.6]). For t1,t2 ∈ C_U, first Z(g,(t1,t2))_U = ⟨Z_*(g)t1,t2⟩ − ⟨Z_*(g)t1,ξ_{t2}⟩ − ⟨Z_*(g)ξ_{t1},t2⟩ + ⟨Z_*(g)ξ_{t1},ξ_{t2}⟩, and the last three terms vanish, so Z(g,(t1,t2))_U = ⟨Z_*(g)_Ut1,t2⟩. Second, ⟨Z_*(g)t1,t2⟩ = −i(Z_*(g)t1,t2) − j(Z_*(g)t1,t2), where i is the horizontal part (finite horizontal intersections plus archimedean Green values) and j the vertical part. Third, j = Σ_v j_v(Z_*(g)t1,t2)log N_v (log N_v = 1 at real v) and j_v(Z_*(g)t1,t2) = ∫_{C_U} j̄_v(Z_*(g)tt1,tt2)dt, with j̄_v the pairing of [YZZ13, §7.1.7]; likewise i_v = ∫_{C_U} ī_v.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 8.6 starts from Z = ⟨Z_*t1,t2⟩ = −i − j, j = Σ_v j_v log N_v and j_v = ∫_{C_U} j̄_v. This rests on the S2 assumption killing the three Hodge-class cross terms. No item states it; height-decomposition-series only mentions it in its proofOutline. Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: ξ̂-admissible arithmetic extension of a divisor on X_{U,O_H}
items.statement: Let D be a divisor on X_{U,H}, where X_{U,O_H} is Q-factorial. Its ξ̂-admissible extension is D̂ = (D̄ + V_D, g_D). Here D̄ is the Zariski closure; V_D is the vertical Q-divisor supported in the special fibres, determined by the condition that D̄ + V_D meets every vertical component as the Hodge class ξ̂ prescribes; and g_D = {g_{D,w}}_{w:H→C} are the admissible Green functions. For CM points the archimedean part is −log‖1_{[β2]}‖_w([β1]) = ī_v(β1,β2), defined by the regularized sum of m_s. The admissible pairing ⟨D̂1,D̂2⟩ for disjoint supports is −(i + j), with i = Σ_v i_v log N_v (horizontal intersections and Green values) and j = D̄1·V_{D2}. For the CM point P over the Hilbert class field H of E, i(1,1) = [H:F]^{-1}⟨P̄,P⟩ = [H:F]^{-1}deg(O(P̄)|_P) with P̄ = (𝒫,g_P).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): The i-part, the j-part (V_{t2} in Lemma 8.9) and the Green function of O(P̄) in Theorem 9.3 are all defined through admissible extensions, which no item defines. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.2 plans admissible pairings, vertical corrections and Green kernels.

items.name: Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization of X_U at a 𝔹-ramified place
items.statement: Let v ∈ Σ_f (𝔹_v a division algebra), U_v maximal, and B = B(v), so B_v ≅ GL2(F_v). Then X_U^an ×_{F_v} F_v^ur ≅ B^×\(Ω ×_{F_v} F_v^ur) × 𝔹_f^×/U. Integrally, X̂_U ×_{Spf O_{F_v}} Spf O_{F_v^ur} ≅ B^×\(Ω̂ ×_{Spf O_{F_v}} Spf O_{F_v^ur}) × 𝔹_f^×/U. Here Ω̂ is Deligne's formal model, obtained by successive blow-ups of P^1_{O_{F_v}}, whose special fibre is a tree of P^1's indexed by GL2(F_v)/F_v^×GL2(O_{F_v}); 𝔹_v^×/U_v ≅ Z via v∘q; and X_U is semistable at v. Hence the irreducible components of the special fibre of X_U above v are indexed by B^×\(GL2(F_v)/F_v^×GL2(O_{F_v})) × 𝔹_f^×/U, and the map to connected components is B^×\𝔹_f^×/U → F_+^×\A_f^×/q(U). If moreover v is inert in E, CM_U = B^×\(B^× ×_{E^×} 𝔹_v^×/U_v) × 𝔹^{v×}_f/U^v embeds by (γ,β) ↦ (γz0, v(q(γ)q(β))), where z0 ∈ Ω̂(O_{E_v}) is the E_v^×-fixed section.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Lemmas 8.8 and 8.9 rest on it: components are indexed by B^×\(GL2(F_v)/F_v^×GL2(O)) × 𝔹_f^×/U, and CM points embed as (γz0, v(q(γ)q(β))). No item states it. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.5 plans it.

items.name: CM points on X_U
items.statement: Fix τ: F ↪ C and the uniformization X_{U,τ}(C) = B(τ)^×\h^± × 𝔹_f^×/U. Let z0 ∈ h be the unique fixed point of E^× under E ↪ B(τ), and write [β]_U = [z0,β]_U. Then P_U = [1]_U, C_U = {[t]_U : t ∈ E^×(A_f)} ≅ E^×\E^×(A_f)/(E^×(A_f)∩U), and CM_U = {[β]_U : β ∈ 𝔹_f^×} ≅ E^×\𝔹_f^×/U. Under the §7.2 hypotheses every point of CM_U is defined over a finite extension of F unramified above Σ(𝔹_f). P_U is defined over the Hilbert class field H of E, and its ramification index in the uniformization is e_P = [E^×∩U:μ_U] = [O_E^×:O_F^×]. Points of C_U are Galois conjugates of P_U. For t ∈ E^×(A_f), t° = [t]_U − ξ_{U,t}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18 (coverage of the paper): Sections 8–9 use C_U ≅ E^×\E^×(A_f)/(E^×(A_f)∩U), CM_U ≅ E^×\𝔹_f^×/U, the field H, and e_P = [O_E^×:O_F^×] throughout. No item in this range defines them; hecke-height-series only uses t°. Another range may already define P_U from §1.2; if so, merge. Route: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.

routes.title: Complex multiplication and explicit reciprocity, Part II: CM heights and Galois-orbit bounds
routes.reason: Reuse the pending Part II ID and title from PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18; its brief explicitly requests the dedicated averaged-Colmez proof from #1143/#1145. Add that proof branch here rather than create a competing CM-height roadmap. The existing quantitative/orbit branches and AGHMP18 alternative proof remain separate consumers/suppliers.
routes.brief:
Augment the already-proposed ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII from PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 with the corrected Yuan–Zhang averaged-Colmez branch; keep its existing quantitative CM-height and Galois-orbit obligations and import them only where actually used. For every CM field E/F with [F:Q]=g prove, for the (2π)^−g squared Faltings metric, 2^−g sum over all CM types h(Φ)=−(1/2)Lf'(0,η)/Lf(0,η)−(1/4)log(dE/F dF). First prove CM component-height invariance, reflex-discriminant decomposition and the nearby-pair average. Replace main Theorem2.7 by the December2022/2023 erratum: good-reduction OE-isogeny with kernel the graph of an OE-isomorphism of relative-different torsion; verify the actual quaternionic lattice kernel. Import Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.1–4), Néron models and semistable abelian varieties (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1), finite flat groups and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/2/4/6), and quaternionic models (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1/2/5). Import the theta representation from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4–6, quadratic Hecke continuation from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1, and the actual local height/Whittaker/adjunction constructions from GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.0/1/2/6/7. Assemble Theorem1.6 and the compact Theorem1.7 and cancel dB; prove existence of the permitted auxiliary incoherent quaternion datum. Preserve the e=[OE*:OF*] factor, normalized orbit averages, p=2 and wild relative differents. Do not duplicate AGHMP18's independent proof or treat the individual Colmez conjecture as proved. Every gap G1–G9 below and source-issue repair remains a design activation gate. Suggested later Lean module: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ComplexMultiplication/AveragedColmez.lean; no Lean file is delivered in this paper job.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-YUAN-ZHANG-18), to respect when stating the layers:
- Theorems 1.6 and 1.7 need U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 ⊇ Ô_E (as p. 576 fixes it). 'U maximal containing Ô_E^×' is weaker when a place of F above 2 with residue field F_2 splits in E, and the step on p. 591 fails there. Choose U this way.
- Theorem 1.6 is proved only for compact X_U (§4.1). Choose the auxiliary 𝔹 with at least two ramified places of F, as Theorem 1.7 requires, and prove that such a datum exists (new item).
- The generator x of O_E ⊗ Z_p in Theorem 2.3, Lemma 2.4 and Corollary 2.6 need not exist (E5). Work over O_σ after enlarging K, with the counting refinement recorded in E5.
- At primes ℘ of F ramified over Q, the τ-quotients W(−) of §5.2 have torsion: 'W(I_y) = 0' fails, the displayed sequences need not be left exact, and Proposition 5.4 and Corollary 5.5 need an integral argument the paper does not give (for example the O_℘-relative Dieudonné theory). The erratum's Proposition 6 has the same gap (E3), and the crystal ranks on p. 569 are right only for the O_℘-relative theory. This is a gate for the proof of Theorem 1.6. Theorem 1.1 itself has an independent proof in PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18.
- The deformation claim before Corollary 5.5 is false as a statement about bare O_{E,p}-modules; Corollary 5.5 follows directly from Proposition 5.4.
- For p = 2 the Breuil–Kisin input of Proposition 5.2 is Kim, Lau and Liu, not [Kis06].
- Theorem 2.7 is replaced by the erratum's Theorem 1; add to its Theorem 2 the step extending O_E-linear automorphisms.

review.reason: Confirmed on the page image; the kind should be 'gap' and affects 'the proof', not 'misprint' and 'nothing'. Counterexample for τ ∈ Hom(E,K): let w | p be ramified over v with F_v = Q_p, p odd, E_w = Q_p(ϖ), ϖ^2 = pu, and let A2 have type Φ2 ∌ τ1. Then Ω(A2)_w ≅ O_K with ϖ acting by τ̄1(ϖ), so Ω(A2,τ1) ≅ O_K/(τ1(ϖ) − τ̄1(ϖ)) = O_K/(2ϖ) ≠ 0, and Ω(A1×A2,τ1) = O_K ⊕ O_K/(2ϖ). Counterexample for the O_F version with F ramified at p: take F_v = Q_p(√p), E_w = F_v ⊗ Q_{p^2} and local type {(id,τ),(Frob,τ′)}. Then Lie is O_K ⊕ O_K with √p acting as (√p, −√p), and its τ-quotient is O_K ⊕ O_K/(2√p). With torsion the printed formula ord_σ(det f*) = ℓ_σΩ(Q,τ) does not hold for torsion-free determinants. In the first example both torsion-free τ1-parts are O_K and are matched by a unit, so the order is 0 while ℓ_σΩ(Q,τ1) = v_σ(2ϖ). The conclusion may still hold, since in this example the τ and τ^c torsion terms are symmetric, but the printed argument does not show it. The root cause is §2.2 of the paper, which calls N(A,τ) a line bundle without making W(A,τ) locally free (range 1). Theorem 1.1 (the averaged Colmez formula itself) is proved independently in [AGHMP18].

The printed argument is complete when Ω(X,τ), Ω(Y,τ), Ω(X^t,τ^c) and Ω(Y^t,τ^c) are locally free; for the O_F version this holds at every σ over a prime unramified in F. sourceIssues.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.7(2) and its proof, case v ∈ S2, pp. 617 and 619
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 8.7(2): 'Let v be a non-archimedean place of F. For any (y,u) ∈ E_v^×× F_v^×, n_{φ_v}(y,u) = φ_v(y,u)·½v(q(y)).' Proof, p. 619: 'If v ∈ S2, the computation is similar, and we will get everywhere 0.'
sourceIssues.correction: For v ∈ S2, write φ_v = ψ1 − (1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2 with ψ1 = 1_{O_{𝔹_v}^×}⊗1_{O^×} and ψ2 = 1_{ϖ_v^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2}⊗1_{O^×}. Then n_{φ_v}(y,u) = −(1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2(y,u) on E_v^××F_v^×, which is not 0; for example n_{φ_v}(1,1) = −1/(1+N_v+N_v²). The printed value is φ_v(1,1)·0 = 0. The lemma is correct for v ∉ S2. Prop. 9.2(2) and Theorem 9.1 still hold, because Lemma 7.6(2) fails at S2 by exactly the compensating amount: c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))ψ2(y,u). Hence d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 2n_{φ_v}log N_v − c_{φ_v} + log|uq(y)|_vφ_v = 0 = −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_vφ_v(y,u). The proof of Prop. 9.2(2) at S2 must use both corrected values.
sourceIssues.reason: Use the formula of Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_{F_v}) (Assumption 7.1), r = 0, so m_ν̄1(n(b)) = 1/(N_v^{−v(b)−1}(N_v−1)) and each shell v(b) = −i contributes 1. For b ∉ O, y·n(b) ∉ GL2(O), so the ψ1 part is 0. For y = diag(a,d), y·n(b) ∈ ϖ^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2 if and only if v(a),v(d) ≥ −1, v(a)+v(d) = 0 and v(ab) ≥ −1. So the upper sum is 1+v(a), the lower 1+v(d), and n_{ψ2} = ½(2+v(ad)) = 1 on supp ψ2|_E. A brute-force enumeration for p = 2 and p = 3 (y = 1, diag(p^{-1},p), diag(p,p^{-1})) gives n = −1/7 and −1/13, against 0 printed. Checked on the page image. Checker 3 found the same error independently (as an out-of-range entry); merge the two. Unchanged in arXiv 1507.06903v3 (checked); not addressed by Erratum5 (Dec 2022), which concerns only Theorem 2.7. Independent second check (checker 3): Apply Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_v) (r = 0): m_{ν1}(n(b)) = 1/(N^{−v(b)−1}(N−1)), so each shell v(b) = −i ≤ −1 contributes 1. ψ1(y n(b)) = 0 for b ∉ O. For y = diag(a,d) with a, d ∈ p^{−1} and ad ∈ O^×, ψ2(y n(b)) = 1 iff v(ab) ≥ −1, which gives v(a)+1 shells; the lower-triangular sum gives v(d)+1; the total is 2 + v(ad) = 2. So n_{ψ2} = 1, and n_{φ_v} = −1/(1+N+N²).

sourceIssues.reason: The Weil index of the norm form of an unramified quadratic extension, taken with respect to ψ_v of conductor d_v^{-1}, is η_v(d_v). Here η_v(u) = 1 for units u, and the index is −1 when F_v/Q_p has odd different exponent, for example at a place above 2 of Q(√2) inert in E.
